articleTitle: PFMRC: A Unified MRC Framework for Chinese Named Entity Recognition via Semantic Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The landscape of natural language processing (NLP) has been revolutionized by advancements that enable the upstream training of knowledge-rich models for downstream tasks, particularly named entity recognition (NER). Traditional NER approaches, treating it as a sequence labeling problem, often fail to deeply understand the whole text and to capture syntactic nuances of text. To address these issues, we introduce PFMRC, a novel machine reading comprehension (MRC) framework that leverages the strengths of both contextual semantics and syntactic information for enhanced NER performance. PFMRC employs a dual-pronged feature extraction strategy, utilizing RoBERTa and BiGRU to encode text features for contextual semantic information and representing them as node features of the graph structure, and a weighted embedding representation to translate syntactic dependencies into graph-structured edge features. Our model further incorporates Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to harmonize node and edge features, facilitating a nuanced understanding of text. The integration of prior knowledge and the modeling of intricate syntactic relationships through Graph Attention Networks (GAT) not only improves entity recognition accuracy but also enriches the feature representation, leading to more robust NER outcomes. Extensive experiments on three Chinese datasets demonstrate PFMRC's superior performance over state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: WTSA: A Whale-enhanced Tree-Seed Algorithm with Timed Iterative Update Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved Tree Seed Optimization Algorithm, namely the Whale Optimization Algorithm with Adaptive Search Strategy (WTSA), designed to address the limitations of traditional Tree Seed Optimization Algorithms. WTSA incorporates an advanced adaptive search mechanism and a dynamic adjustment framework to enhance the balance between exploration and exploitation, overcoming issues such as premature convergence and entrapment in local optima. The algorithm adopts an Iterative Chaos Initialization strategy, combining deterministic and stochastic methods to achieve a more uniform and diversified initial population distribution. Additionally, WTSA introduces a dynamic search step-size adjustment, significantly improving convergence speed and solution quality. The integration of multi-strategy search methods enables WTSA to effectively navigate complex search spaces and identify global optima. Through extensive comparative experiments with advanced algorithms, including the original Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and TSA variants, the results demonstrate WTSA’s superior performance in solution accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings highlight WTSA’s robustness and versatility in solving various optimization problems, making it a competitive choice for complex real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Global Initial Pose Estimation Method for Mobile Robots Based on Magnetic Matching and 2D LiDAR Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the increasing demand for indoor global localization in the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) denial environments, accurate initial pose estimation has become crucial, as it forms the foundation for subsequent trajectory tracking. To address the challenges of infrastructure dependence, high sensor costs, and large data volumes in current indoor localization research, we propose a global initial pose estimation method based on magnetic matching and 2D LiDAR line features. After constructing the magnetic map and grid occupancy map of the environment, the method first uses magnetic information for coarse localization. Then, line features from LiDAR point clouds and the scene are extracted for angular estimation. Finally, the pose is refined using corner points. This approach enables accurate initial pose estimation of a mobile robot at any location within a global map. The algorithm was tested in an indoor corridor environment, with an average position estimation accuracy of 0.164 m and an average angular accuracy of 1.7°.

articleTitle: HTSA: A Hybrid Tree Seed Algorithm based on Differential Evolution with Dynamic Population Diversity Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Based on the problem of Tree Seed Algorithm (TSA), this paper proposes a Hybrid Tree Seed Algorithm (Hybrid-Tree Seed Algorithm, HTSA) based on Differential Evolution and Dynamic Population Diversity Maintenance. HTSA effectively overcomes the limitations of the original TSA by introducing key enhancement mechanisms. By combining Bernoulli mapping initialization, HTSA ensures that the population distribution is more balanced and efficient compared to the stochastic mapping of TSA. Moreover, the introduction of a positional update formula inspired by the Sparrow Search Algorithm in the seed updating enhances population diversity and convergence, especially in the late optimization stages. Integration with Differential Evolution (DE) further enhances global exploration capabilities. Together, these modifications address issues such as premature convergence and sensitivity to local optimal values in TSA.Comparative experiments showed that HTSA outperformed TSA,EST-TSA and other benchmark algorithms, showing significant advantages in optimization power, convergence rate and population diversity.

articleTitle: Research on variable step-size CMA algorithm in mode-division multiplexing system
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of contradiction between the convergence speed and steady-state error of the traditional Constant Modulus Algorithm (CMA) algorithm in channel equalization of Mode Division Multiplexing (MDM) system, a variable step-size CMA algorithm based on Sigmoid function, mode coupling theory and power coupling theory was proposed. In order to verify the optimization effect, a 6×6 mode-division multiplexing system model based on strong coupling was built by using the power coupling theory. the traditional CMA algorithm and the improved variable step-size algorithm were used to balance the data at the receiver. The results show that the improved variable step-size algorithm has a performance gain of 1.5dB compared with the traditional CMA algorithm when the FEC (Forward Error Correction) threshold is 3.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, the average convergence speed and steady-state error of the six channels are gained.

articleTitle: Hybrid Multi-Modal Recommendation System: Integrating MMOE and XGBoost for Enhanced Personalization and Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the field of computer vision, 6D object detection and pose estimation are critical for applications such as robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. Traditional methods often struggle with achieving high accuracy in both object detection and precise pose estimation simultaneously. This study proposes an improved 6D object detection and pose estimation pipeline based on the existing 6D-VNet framework, enhanced by integrating a Hybrid Task Cascade (HTC) and a High-Resolution Network (HRNet) backbone. By leveraging the strengths of HTC's multi-stage refinement process and HRNet's ability to maintain high-resolution representations, our approach significantly improves detection accuracy and pose estimation precision. Furthermore, we introduce advanced post-processing techniques and a novel model integration strategy that collectively contribute to superior performance on public and private benchmarks. Our method demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art models, making it a valuable contribution to the domain of 6D object detection and pose estimation.

articleTitle: F2MSA2: Integrating Mamba and Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Sequential Recommendation (SR) has been widely used in various Internet platforms, such as content streaming platforms and e-commerce. While the Self-Attention (SA) mechanism has been shown to be effective in capturing global dependencies, its quadratic complexity makes it less efficient. Mamba can improve efficiency, but its unidirectional architecture makes it difficult to capture the full context of a sequence, preventing further development.To address these issues, this work proposes a sequential recommendation model called F2MSA2 This model combines Mamba and SA for hybrid modelling. A modified version of the Mamba block, flipped Mamba (FMA), is first introduced, which flips the interaction sequences and then serves as an input to the Mamba block to enhance the model's ability to acquire and utilize future information. Secondly frequency-domain SA (FSA) transforms the SA from the time domain to the frequency domain in order to acquire both low-frequency and high-frequency information, where the low-frequency information usually reflects the user's long-term stable preferences while the high-frequency information reveals the user's short-term fast-changing interests. And several frequency-domain feed-forward networks are constructed to learn external factors and mitigate their effects on user preferences.

articleTitle: Limb-Constraint Based Spatial-Temporal Collaborative Network for Enhanced 3D Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Recently, methods that combine Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Transformers have demonstrated superior performance in 3D human pose estimation. However, they merely fuse captured local and global features simplistically, failing to reasonably constrain the inherent limb structure information of the human body. In this paper, we propose a novel spatial-temporal collaborative network architecture that acquires the positional information of 3D human pose through GCNs and Transformer pathways, and integrates a limb constraint module to correct errors caused by the human body's spatial-temporal variations, thereby enhancing the accuracy of 3D human pose estimation. We evaluate our model on two popular benchmark datasets: Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP, achieving a significant improvement in the accuracy of 3D human pose estimation, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based CT Image Classification Model with Application to COVID-19 Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the computed tomography (CT) images, a deep learning (DL)-based classification model is proposed, which is applied to realize the accurate diagnosis of the novel coronavirus disease COVID-19. In particular, the ResNeXt is adopted as the backbone, where the grouped convolution facilitates the extraction of discriminative features, and the residual structure can effectively address the gradient vanishing problem. Moreover, by improving and introducing the residual block in ResNet-D, the network can flexibly pay attention to features with different importance. Named as ResNeXt-vd, the proposed model is proven competitive in COVID-19 diagnosis task, which outperforms some other classic DL models by yielding the highest accuracy of 0.975, thereby showing the potential application values in providing reliable diagnostic references for the clinicians.

articleTitle: Enriched Mandarin Social Media Dataset for Sentiment Features Problem Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a crucial text classification task that aims to extract, process, and analyze opinions, sentiments, and subjectivity within texts. This dataset is a secondary dataset from the public Chinese IT technology exchange platform website CSDN, the data originates from Baidu waimai (now called Ele. me). Each comment in the data set is re-annotated manually using sentiment labels (positive, negative, or neutral), and 13 types of labels such as word order, polysemy, cyberword, argot, irony, typing errors, context, word segmentation wrong, emojis, Chinglish or mixed Chinese and English, polyphone, omission of characters, phonetic alphabet, abbreviation are used to annotate issues that affect Chinese mandarin sentiment. These re-annotations have been validated by a Mandarin linguist. This paper proposes an enhanced system model for Mandarin sentiment analysis of social media text based on transformer encoder. Researchers and developers can utilize this dataset to train sentiment analysis models, natural language processing algorithms, machine learning, or deep learning systems to accurately identify and analyze the sentiments expressed by consumers on Mandarin social media platforms.

articleTitle: Multi-Region Attention Residual Network-Based Crop Row Detection For Agricultural Robot Field Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the context of real-world agricultural settings, robots frequently encounter uneven terrain when navigating through tilled fields. Such irregularities can lead to the robot drifting off course. To achieve effective autonomous navigation for agricultural robots, it is crucial to develop strategies for accurately detecting crop rows to mitigate the impact of external disturbances. In this paper, a novel algorithm of crop row detection for field robots that incorporates a multi-head attention mechanism and Res-Net model is presented (MRA-ResNet). First, real-time field video captured by an agricultural robot is processed for frame extraction to obtain a large number of images, which are initially convolved by an adaptive threshold filter to obtain key frame features. Then, the crop features in the field are learned by setting up a multi-region attention module, segmenting the crop and background, and dividing the learned crop feature images into several vertical image strips. These learned vertical image strips are then mapped to the low latitude for classification by vertical projection and MRA-ResNet. Finally, the center-line of the crop rows is further determined accurately. The experimental results show that MRA-ResNet can well realize crop row detection in the field.

articleTitle: Fabric defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8s
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the fabric manufacturing industry, various unfavorable factors often lead to fabric defects. However, current systems face issues such as multi-scale defects and loss of information on tiny objects, resulting in low target detection accuracy and high missed detection rates. Based on the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8s algorithm to detect fabric defects. By integrating the DCNv3 operator into the C2f module of YOLOv8s's backbone network, the C2f-DCNv3 module is successfully constructed. This improvement enhances the model's ability to model geometric transformations and contextual information, thereby better capturing spatial deformations and contextual details. Experiments conducted on the Tianchi Fabric Defect Detection dataset reveal that compared to the original YOLOv8s, the algorithm proposed in this paper achieves a 3.14% improvement in the mAP@0.5 metric. The algorithm presented in this paper achieves efficient and accurate defect recognition, demonstrating superior performance across various fabric types and complex backgrounds.

articleTitle: A Novel PCB Defect Detection Network Based on the Improved YOLOv8 with Fusion of Hybrid Attention Transformer and Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The quality of the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) directly affects the performance and reliability of the electronic product. However, PCB defect detection still faces challenges in terms of high precision and real-time performance in automated inspection until now. In this article, a novel PCB defect detection network based on the improved YOLOv8 named YOLO-HB is proposed, which integrates Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) and Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN). The proposed PCB defect detection network have the dual advantages of good real-time performance and high detection accuracy in the task of PCB defect detection. The experiments conducted on two well-known PCB defect detection public datasets, PCB_DATASET and DeepPCB, show that the results significantly outperform the original YOLOv8 model and also surpass other classic object detection models.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Real-time Multi-sensor Fusion State Estimation Method Based on Event Camera in Challenging Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: State estimation refers to the integration of sensor input and observation information to estimate the current state of a robot, such as its position and orientation. However, achieving robust and accurate state estimation in challenging scenarios remains an urgent problem to solve. In this paper, we propose a novel Event-Visual-Inertial Odometry (EVIO) method that tightly couples event data, standard images, and inertial measurements. This method fully leverages the excellent complementary characteristics of multi-sensor fusion to estimate the ego-motion of sensors in challenging scenarios such as High Dynamic Range (HDR), low light, and motion blur caused by vigorous motion. In challenging benchmark experiments, our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 16%, and this achievement does not rely on extensive manual parameter tuning. Lastly, we qualitatively demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of our method for real-time state estimation across different scales and types of challenging scenarios.

articleTitle: Sentence-Guided Comment Tree Fusion for Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The rapid spread of fake news significantly impacts social cognition and media credibility, making the effective detection of fake news a critical issue. This paper proposes a fake news detection method based on a comment tree structure. By constructing a hierarchical comment tree and integrating cosine similarity filtering with a cross-attention mechanism, the method optimizes the comment selection process. Finally, a gated mechanism is employed to fuse the features of news sentences and comment information, thereby improving the accuracy of fake news detection. Experiments conducted on two public datasets, FakeNewsNet and BuzzFace, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant performance improvements in fake news detection compared to baseline models.

articleTitle: Personalized federated meta-learning based on dynamic clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Due to the issues of poor convergence on highly heterogeneous data and the lack of personalized solutions faced by traditional Federated Learning (FL), Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) has emerged as a current research hotspot and trend. PFL aims to provide customized models for each client by considering the data characteristics and requirements of different clients (or devices), thereby enhancing model accuracy and practicality. Meta-learning has become one of the key technologies for realizing PFL due to its rapid adaptation capabilities. By learning how to effectively adjust and optimize learning algorithms from historical tasks, meta-learning enables PFL systems to more quickly adapt to new clients and datasets. However, in scenarios with heterogeneous data, a single global model approach in meta-learning may struggle to achieve good performance. In this work, we propose a dynamic clustering-based personalized federated meta-learning framework (C2FML), which clusters clients based on the low-dimensional representations of their data participating in training during each iteration. Subsequently, within each cluster, the model updates obtained through meta-learning using local data from clients belonging to that cluster are aggregated to obtain a personalized model for that cluster, which is then distributed to the respective clients. This way, each client obtains a dedicated personalized model upon completion of training. Our research ensures that each group consists of clients with similar data distributions, which facilitates model learning in multitask scenarios and accelerates model convergence. By doing so, the proposed framework can be applied in highly heterogeneous environments, and we evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on public datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art federated meta-learning, our proposed framework achieves improved model accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multi-vessel Trajectory Prediction Using a Multiscale Hypergraph Neural Network: Capturing Complex Maritime Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Marine transportation constitutes a vital component in the operation of the global economy. Recent global crises have profoundly disrupted maritime transportation, escalating costs, reducing connectivity, and intensifying global economic and supply chain challenges. The accurate prediction of vessel trajectories is crucial for optimizing operational efficiency, enhancing safety measures, and minimizing maritime costs. In this study, the application of a multiscale hypergraph neural network to multi-vessel trajectory prediction is proposed, aiming to model complex interactions between vessels at both the pair-wise and group levels. This model enhances prediction accuracy by capturing maritime-specific relational dynamics, which can improve navigational safety and efficiency. Compared to Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE), the model demonstrates superior path prediction performance, achieving the best results in terms of a number of key metrics. This showcases its strong potential for applications in multi-vessel trajectory prediction.

articleTitle: Autonomous Trajectory Tracking Control Strategy of an Aerial Robot under Large Maneuver
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Large maneuver flights of aerial robots are essential in practical missions, allowing them to avoid obstacles and perform tasks efficiently. This paper presents an autonomous trajectory tracking control strategy design of an aerial robot under large maneuver, ensuring the tacking accuracy and demonstrating effectiveness in real-flight tests. First, dynamics modeling and large maneuver trajectory design are presented. Next, the control strategy is developed with an inner-loop attitude controller and L1 control based outer-loop position controller. Finally, simulation experiment quantitively shows the designed strategy’s ability to achieve precise trajectory tracking under large maneuver, and real-flight tests further demonstrates the controller’s effectiveness in practical missions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Intelligent Hotel Room Resource Allocation Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In light of the accelerated advancement of intelligent hospitality establishments, the effective distribution of room resources has emerged as a pivotal research area, with the objective of enhancing operational efficacy and customer satisfaction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel room resource allocation optimisation model based on deep learning, which builds upon the existing Transformer architecture. In particular, an enhanced Transformer model has been devised, which incorporates the time embedding module into the network architecture in order to capture the temporal dynamic characteristics of customer booking behaviour. Furthermore, the ability to identify key features has been enhanced by introducing a weighted self-attention mechanism. Furthermore, the model output layer incorporates a multi-objective optimisation strategy, which serves to balance the relationship between customer satisfaction and hotel revenue. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior performance in terms of room utilisation, resource allocation efficiency and customer satisfaction when compared to the traditional method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control Based on A Modified Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Reinforcement learning has been shown to effectively optimize traffic signal timing. This study focuses on reducing vehicle fuel consumption and introduces an adaptive traffic signal control model, termed MPPO_TSC. This model incorporates various algorithmic enhancements over the standard Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) framework and integrates both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to improve the capability of deep neural networks in extracting features from dynamic traffic flows. Additionally, to overcome the challenge of agents being unable to access real-time vehicle fuel consumption data, this study devises an approximate method for estimating differential fuel consumption and develops a novel reward function accordingly. Experimental validation was carried out on the SUMO simulation platform, with tests conducted in both simulated and real-world intersection scenarios. The results indicate that MPPO_TSC achieves reductions in average fuel consumption per vehicle and decreases in average waiting time compared to the four control strategies.

articleTitle: Performance Study of Sea Surface Ultraviolet Communication Based on Circular Polarization Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) communication is widely used for communication between vessels on the sea surface due to its high level of security. However, the communication performance is less than ideal due to the significant atmospheric turbulence and scattering effects over the sea surface. In this study, we effectively fit the parameters of sea surface atmospheric turbulence by adjusting the scale parameter of atmospheric turbulence and propose a high-computation-efficiency scattering model based on Monte Carlo simulation with partial uniform sampling (MCS-PUS) to simulate the atmospheric channel over the sea surface. Taking advantage of the characteristic that the polarization state of the laser in the atmospheric channel is less affected by surrounding factors, we demonstrate that the circular polarization modulation system can significantly improve communication performance and enhance the computation efficiency by a factor of 1.35×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> compared to the original algorithm. Finally, by comparing the bit error rate (BER) with the mainstream On-Off Keying (OOK) modulation method, we show that circular polarization modulation can effectively mitigate the impact of atmospheric turbulence and scattering effects on optical signals, reducing the system’s BER by one order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Construction of a Cognitive Graph for Intelligent Manufacturing Robot Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The forms of tasks in intelligent manufacturing are diverse, and their operating environment is also dynamically changing. Effective knowledge representation and reasoning are key foundations for enhancing robots' understanding and execution capabilities of complex tasks. Therefore, this article constructs a cognitive graph of robot behavior in the field of intelligent manufacturing based on BERT-BiLSTM-CRF. Firstly, based on the multi-level requirements in robotic operation, a robot behavior corpus is constructed, and the robotic behavior ontology layers Task, Skill, Action, Location, Agent (H), and Object are defined to standardize the semantic structure of behavior. Then, using the BERT model to extract language structure and semantic relationship information, deep-level feature representations are obtained from the text; Capture contextual semantic relationships of behavior through the BiLSTM network, and combine the CRF model to globally constrain and optimize the predicted behavior results. Finally, the extracted triplets are stored using neo4j to form a cognitive graph of intelligent manufacturing robot behavior (IMRBCG). The experimental results show that the P, R, and F1-score of the proposed method are 95.51%, 90.66%, and 93.02%, respectively, effectively extracting 8763 behavioral triplets. This cognitive graph provides technical support for the task of the use of planning and collaboration for intelligent manufacturing robots.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive On-Demand Assistive Control Strategy for Upper Limb Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Currently, upper limb exoskeleton rehabilitation robots provide the same level of assistance to different patients during active rehabilitation training, which prevents patients from fully utilizing their own initiative and thus affects the rehabilitation effect. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive on-demand assistive control strategy based on impedance control for upper limbs. By establishing two modules of on-demand assistive control and trajectory tracking control, combined with methods of assessing limb movement state and on-demand control to adapt to the needs of patients at different stages of rehabilitation, the system achieves automatic adjustment of the assistive force size through synovial control, thereby maximizing the patient's moment of main force. The experimental results show that the adaptive assistive force system, compared with traditional methods, provides an average assistive force that is reduced by 41.9% under the same limb movement state coefficient, and can gradually reduce the assistive force provided according to the patient's recovery of motor ability. This indicates that the method is highly adaptable to different patients and can effectively enhance the patient's initiative in rehabilitation training, thereby improving the rehabilitation effect.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Multi-Stage BERT Fusion Framework with Dual Attention for Enhanced Cyberbullying Detection in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Detecting and classifying cyberbullying in social media is hard because of the complex nature of online language and the changing nature of content. This study presents a multi-stage BERT fusion framework. It uses hierarchical embeddings, dual attention mechanisms, and extra features to improve detection of cyberbullying content. The framework combines BERT embeddings with features like sentiment and topic information. It uses self-attention and cross-attention to align features and has a hierarchical classification head for multi-category classification. A dynamic loss balancing strategy helps optimize learning and improves accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. These results show the model’s strong performance and potential for broader use in analyzing social media content.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning for Accurate Classification of Wild Mushrooms: A Hybrid ResNet and Region-Based CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Accurate mushroom classification is essential for applications ranging from ecological research to foraging safety. This study proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) based approach for multi-class mushroom classification, aiming to address the unique challenges posed by diverse morphological features across mushroom species. Utilizing an expanded dataset of nine classes, this model was trained and evaluated with various metrics, including accuracy, F1score, ROC-AUC, and a detailed analysis of confusion matrices, to assess performance across class boundaries. Future improvements will focus on expanding the dataset to include more diverse samples, implementing classspecific training weights, and further refining CNN layers to enhance feature extraction. These advancements will address current limitations and improve the model’s generalizability and robustness, underscoring its potential as a robust tool for mushroom classification applications.

articleTitle: Bridging Sentence and Document Contexts: A PEFT-Enhanced Framework for Document-Level Neural Machine Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Document-level neural machine translation (DNMT) faces challenges in integrating context and maintaining semantic consistency. This paper proposes a coarse-to-fine semantic transfer approach that captures both fine-grained and coarse-grained document-level context. By employing a two-stage training strategy with Adapter-enhanced modules, the method ensures effective semantic adaptation from sentence to document levels. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate significant improvements in s-BLEU and d-BLEU metrics, outperforming existing approaches.

articleTitle: Research and Prospects of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Traffic Surveillance and Emergency Response in Multiple Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The road safety problem caused by traffic accidents(a pileup, overspeed collision, drunk driving collisions and so on.) has always been a hot topic, which seriously threatens the social stability and economic development. The traditional methods of traffic state detection are mainly manual check or identification of relevant traffic parameters by road side cameras. These methods generally have the disadvantages of low efficiency, slow speed, low accuracy and slow data processing. So, equipment that can detect quickly and accurately is needed. Compared with traditional methods, Uavs are highly mobile and flexible, and with the continuous improvement of computer processing power, the combination of the two will have great application advantages in accident handling, order management, traffic guidance, and vehicle flow detection. Combined with the current situation of UAV traffic monitoring, this paper summarizes the research progress of UAV in traffic monitoring, and looks forward to the future research and development trend.

articleTitle: Analysis of Traditional Chinese Medicine Health Data based on Data Mining: Constitution Classification and Personalized Wellness Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The tenets of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) place considerable emphasis on the significance of individual physique classification and the necessity of personalised health management. This study proposes an innovative framework based on data mining, utilising a single deep learning model, the Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM), in conjunction with a number of optimisation techniques, for the classification of TCM health data and the generation of personalised health recommendations. The introduction of adaptive learning rate adjustment and regularisation strategies enabled the optimisation of the model training process and the improvement of the model's generalisation ability through the reduction of overfitting and the merging of components. Additionally, the feature selection technique was employed to extract the most representative physique-related features, and the classification effect was further optimised by the weighted loss function. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior performance in terms of accuracy in constitution classification and recommendation effectiveness when compared to the traditional method.

articleTitle: Design of Visualization Simulation Software for Collaborative Formation Control of Mobile Robot Cluster
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Simulation tools are important auxiliary tools for scientific research. Design method of a practical and convenient simulation software for visual simulation of collaborative formation control for mobile robot cluster was discussed in this paper. The simulation software was designed in two main parts: human-computer interaction and visualization display of algorithm simulation. The software was implemented based on Qt development platform and some key methods of design and implementation involved were detailed. The simulation results of this software under different formation control algorithms are shown to demonstrate its practicality and flexibility in applications.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Measurement Uncertainty for Distributed Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The distributed measurement system (DMS) is a representative measurement system with multiple transmitters. One of essential indexes used to evaluate the overall performance of DMS is measurement uncertainty. In this paper, a model of measurement uncertainty for DMS is derived explicitly, and the anisotropy and inhomogeneity of measurement uncertainty along different axes are analyzed in detail. The effect of various layouts of transmitters on measurement uncertainty is also discussed by carrying out simulation experiment and validation experiment. The experimental results show that for the layout of transmitters, the deployment in type of ‘4-trapezoid’ is superior to that in type of ‘2-line’, ‘3-line’, ‘3-triangle’, ‘4-squre’, and ‘4-line’, especially in terms of measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: A Low-Light Image Enhancement Method Combining Attention Mechanism and Retinex Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) faces difficulties arising from issues like color distortion and noise in low-light environments. Specifically, the underexposed areas of an image often contain more noise than the normally exposed regions. In this paper, we introduce an enhancement algorithm that leverages a channel attention mechanism, enabling effective extraction of key features from low-light images while filtering out irrelevant information to improve overall image quality. Furthermore, to boost image recovery and assist with the Retinex decomposition process, we propose a light smoothing loss function, which enhances the image's structural boundaries. Through extensive experimental assessments, it is evident that the approach we propose exceeds the performance of current leading unsupervised methods.

articleTitle: Application and Practice of Inter Domain Fault Localization Technology in Open Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: For devices that support open optical networks, a technology for solving fault location problems in cross-domain scenarios is proposed. It uses optical module tone modulation to create unoccupied register space for status code reporting, ensuring accurate information transmission through a robust docking and response mechanism. By establishing inter-domain communication, periodic messages allow local modules to access remote module connection status, providing essential data for fault location. A unified YANG model standardizes data reporting for-mats across manufacturers, and telemetry technology is employed for performance reporting, supporting rapid data acquisition and reducing redundancy to improve efficiency. Status codes are encapsulated in local module performance data for stable reporting. Fault location is pinpointed by analyzing status codes, with root cause analysis providing clear solutions. Simulations with 100GBASR-LR4 modules confirm the technology's accuracy and timeliness, significantly improving fault location speed and precision in open optical networks.

articleTitle: An adaptive density clustering algorithm based on measurement parameters and representative points
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: DBSCAN clustering algorithm (Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise) is a density-based spatial clustering algorithm with noise. Due to its insensitivity to noise and its ability to cluster irregularly shaped data without specifying the number of clusters , it has been widely used. However, at the same time, DBSCAN also has some problems such as excessive dependence on input parameters, cumbersome parameter adjustment and poor clustering performance for samples with uneven density. To solve the problems in DBSCAN, the MR-DBSCANS algorithm (Adaptive density clustering algorithm based on measurement parameters and representative points) is proposed according to the newly proposed parameter adaptive dynamic selection method and representative point reallocation strategy. Firstly, constructing measurement parameters based on compactness and penalty terms. Secondly, using measurement parameters to filter noise points and core points, and selecting effective neighborhood radius(Eps), the sample density judgment threshold (MinPts), and optimal neighborhood points for the core points. Then the DBSCAN redistribution strategy based on representative points is proposed, and the clustering results will be revised through the redistribution strategy, to obtain the correct clustering results. Finally, the adaptability and clustering performance of the MR-DBSCAN algorithm are simulated and verified in the dataset

articleTitle: Research on microseismic source localization based on improved particle swarm optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Accurate microseismic source localization is crucial for detecting potential geological hazards during mining operations, ensuring the safe and efficient progress of excavation activities. The accuracy and reliability of source localization are closely linked to the selection of appropriate algorithms. While the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm offers the advantage of fast convergence, it is prone to premature convergence and low localization accuracy when directly applied to source localization. To address these issues, this study employs chaotic mapping to replace traditional methods for initializing the particle population, enhancing population diversity. The proposed method is validated through engineering case studies. The results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional PSO algorithm, the chaotic mapping-based improved PSO algorithm achieves faster convergence and superior optimization capabilities, making it suitable for solving practical engineering problems.

articleTitle: FCHANet: Feature Cross Hierarchical Fusion Attention Network for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision, and deep learning has led to significant advancements in recent years. However, existing methods still struggle with accurate localization and recognition, particularly when detecting objects across multiple scales and varying appearances. These challenges are primarily due to limitations in feature aggregation and fusion techniques. To address these issues, FCHA-Net is proposed, a novel network that utilizes Biformer as the backbone and incorporates two key modules, HAM and FCAF, at the neck. The HAM module enhances multi-scale feature aggregation, enabling better capture of object details across different sizes. The FCAF module applies a cross-attention mechanism to fuse multi-scale features, preserving fine-grained information and improving the accuracy of feature fusion. The combination of these two modules provides an effective solution to the multi-scale detection problem. Training conducted with the MMDetection framework on the PASCAL VOC dataset highlights that FCHA-Net achieves a 93.2% mean average precision (mAP).Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the HAM and FCAF modules, demonstrating FCHA-Net’s strength in multi-scale feature fusion and information retention. These results introduce a promising approach to improving object detection and offer new insights for future advancements in the field.

articleTitle: Blend of VADER and TextBlob for Movie Script Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper compares two sentiment analysis models: VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) and TextBlob on the classification of movie scripts. The scripts were rated as G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17 which are standard MPAA ratings. Further, the work also extended the use of the blended score that combined the weighted results from VADER and TextBlob to reach higher accuracy, using certain features such as profanity scores. It talks about the working mechanism of VADER and TextBlob in application to the English movie scripts. The paper critically reviews the literature of methodologies pertaining to sentiment analysis, presents some practical experiments that establish the efficiency of our approach, and concludes with the correlation analysis of the sentiment scores between VADER and TextBlob while suggesting further research directions for multilingual sentiment analysis. While BERT and RoBERTa are really accurate, VADER and TextBlob have their merits in simplicity and computational efficiency, offering speed whereby prototyping is possible; hence, these would be better positioned for use against smaller datasets and resource-poor environments. Coupled with their interpretability, features like these make them quite good for movie script analyses, hence being able to get suitable insight into sentiment without heaviness due to higher-order models. A balancing act between the two sides will make the tools apt for this study: VADER and TextBlob.

articleTitle: Program Design and Application of Automatic Identification System Data Fusion with Optical Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to design the data fusion program of Automatic Identification System (AIS)+optical remote sensing, adopt the mode of remote sensing satellite platform carrying AIS system payload and optical payload, carry out the sea observation of AIS+optical remote sensing, and realize the fusion of the shore-based AIS data with the satellite AIS data and the optical remote sensing data, so as to make up for the short board of the current maritime supervision and service capability.

articleTitle: Dynamic camouflage generation using online learning in conditional GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Traditional camouflage designs rely mainly on manual experience and fail to integrate environmental textures effectively, nor do they adequately consider the complexity and diversity of battlefield backgrounds. In light of this, this paper introduces a dynamic camouflage generation method based on an online learning with conditional GANs. This method uses online learning algorithm to train the model and combines style loss, pixel loss, color distribution loss, adversarial loss, and patch discriminator to ensure the generation effect, which can produce high-quality camouflage patterns from background images. To assess the effectiveness of the generated images, we calculated the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) between them and real samples, achieving a score of 11.08. Additionally, we measured the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) between the generated camouflage patterns and their corresponding backgrounds, which resulted in a value of 0.89. It indicates the successful camouflage effect of the generated patterns. Moreover, by integrating these camouflage patterns into background images and analyzing their blending with the backgrounds using the Canny detector, we further validate the efficacy of the generated camouflage patterns produced by this model.

articleTitle: Research on fault diagnosis and analysis of AC relays based on CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Relay detection is an important step to ensure the reliable operation of relays in electrical systems. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis system for alternating current(AC) relays based on Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN). The system uses a vibration sensor to collect signals from the AC relay, and then transmits the vibration signals to the edge processing unit embedded with CNN. The edge processing unit extracts the time domain features of the AC relay vibration signal, and then classifies the features in the CNN model. Finally, the system outputs the results of abnormal vibration detection. The experimental results show that the system proposed in this paper can effectively identify the abnormal vibration of AC relays, reaching an accuracy rate of 98.3%, which is better than the traditional Support Vector Machines(SVM) or Random Forest(RF) methods. This paper provides a standardized, automated and intelligent solution for the field of abnormal vibration detection of AC relays, which helps to improve product quality and production efficiency.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-Transformer Architecture for Noise Cancellation in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper proposes a speech enhancement algorithm that fuses a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a Transformer. It aims to effectively suppress background interference in complex noise environments and improve the clarity and intelligibility of speech signals. A weighted source-to-distortion ratio (wSDR) loss function is used to obtain the training gradient of the balanced model against the speech and noise signals by adjusting the parameter alpha. The results of the verification on the AISHELL-1 dataset show that the CNN+Transformer model has achieved an average PESQ score of 2.518 and an STOI score of 0.7234 under most test conditions.

articleTitle: OpenRAG: Open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation Architecture for Personalized Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper introduces OpenRAG, an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system architecture designed to enhance GenAI applications in personalized learning. The architecture is modular with loosely coupled components: Generator, User Interface, Indexing subsystem, Retriever, and Orchestration module. The research applies cutting-edge design patterns for retrieval, generation, indexing, storage, user interactions, and performance optimization, whereas the data flow and processing pipeline are seamlessly integrated for customization and adaptability. A case study demonstrates a proof-of-concept implementation of OpenRAG used in an online learning platform, resulting in significant increases in learner engagement and education efficiency. Key design concerns such as computational efficiency, content accuracy, learning styles, and user experience are discussed along with their solutions.

articleTitle: Allocation of UAV-Assisted Cognitive Vehicle Network Resources Under Malicious Jamming: A Hierarchical Game Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: UAV has the characteristics of easy deployment and flexible mobility, which can provide effective and reliable communication services for cognitive vehicle networking. However, the open communication environment makes UAV vulnerable to malicious interference attacks when providing services to vehicle users, and the communication resources provided to users are limited. The communication performance of the entire network will be greatly affected. In this paper, the anti-interference resource allocation of UAV-assisted cognitive vehicle network under malicious interference attack is studied. Due to the complexity of the problem, it cannot be solved directly. The objective optimization problem is decomposed into two sub-problems, and a two-layer game algorithm is proposed based on the characteristics of the problem. First, Stackelberg game is used to solve the position deployment problem of the UAV, achieve the optimal connection between the UAV and the vehicle, and resist the jamming attack. Second, channel allocation is carried out by using potential game, and the effect of co-channel interference is reduced. The simulation results show that the whole system can achieve higher performance than the existing algorithm. And can achieve a higher transmission rate in the jamming environment.

articleTitle: An Fusion Algorithm of Improved A-star and DWA for Autonomous Vehicle Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the need for global path optimization and dynamic real-time obstacle avoidance in unknown environments for autonomous vehicles, we propose an autonomous vehicle path planning scheme that integrates an optimized A-star algorithm with the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA). The A-star algorithm is capable of finding the global optimal path. By optimizing the A-star algorithm, an adaptive heuristic function is introduced, key path points are selected, and redundant path points are removed. Finally, the Dynamic Window Approach is integrated to achieve dynamic real-time obstacle avoidance in complex environments. Comparative simulation experiments conducted in MATLAB demonstrate that the improved algorithm optimizes trajectory length, trajectory smoothness, and elapsed time. It meets the requirements of global optimization and dynamic real-time obstacle avoidance, providing a superior path planning solution.

articleTitle: Robustness of Large Language Models Against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The increasing deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in various applications necessitates a rigorous evaluation of their robustness against adversarial attacks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive study on the robustness of GPT LLM family. We employ two distinct evaluation methods to assess their resilience. The first method introduces character-level text attack in input prompts, testing the models on three sentiment classification datasets: StanfordNLP/IMDB, Yelp Reviews, and SST-2. The second method involves using jailbreak prompts to challenge the safety mechanisms of the LLMs. Our experiments reveal significant variations in the robustness of these models, demonstrating their varying degrees of vulnerability to both character-level and semantic-level adversarial attacks. These findings underscore the necessity for improved adversarial training and enhanced safety mechanisms to bolster the robustness of LLMs.

articleTitle: Consistency Adversarial Training for Robust Decision Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose a significant threat to the security of deep learning systems. While Adversarial Training (AT) has emerged as a prominent defense strategy, traditional AT methods focus primarily on training with loss-maximizing adversarial samples, potentially overlooking decision boundary refinement. To address this limitation, we propose Consistency Adversarial Training (CAT), a novel approach that shifts the focus of AT from the endpoint of the attack trajectory to its intersection with the decision boundary. CAT innovates by aligning adversarial samples at decision boundary intersections with their corresponding "ancestor" samples, thereby establishing a more comprehensive defense mechanism. Through extensive experiments and ablation studies, we demonstrate that CAT promotes the formation of a flatter and more precise loss landscape, thereby improving the robustness of neural networks.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Listwise Reranking with Large Language Models in Limited-Resource Language Contexts
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant effectiveness across various NLP tasks, including text ranking. This study assesses the performance of large language models (LLMs) in listwise reranking for limited-resource African languages. We compare proprietary models RankGPT3.5, Rank4o-mini, RankGPTo1-mini and RankClaude-sonnet in cross-lingual contexts. Results indicate that these LLMs significantly outperform traditional baseline methods such as BM25-DT in most evaluation metrics, particularly in nDCG@10 and MRR@100. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs in enhancing reranking tasks for low-resource languages and offer insights into cost-effective solutions.

articleTitle: Multimodal emotion recognition based on audiovisual text
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The article constructs a hybrid fusion model for multimodal emotion recognition. First, facial expression features are extracted using Mediapipe and OpenCV, and then a convolutional neural network, bi-directional long and short-term memory combined with SelfAttention mechanism network model (CNN-BiLSTM - SelfAttention) is used to train for the expression features; the speech part of the paper uses an LSTM model to train the audio features; and the text part of the paper extracts Chinese text features with the help of the Roberta model. Roberta model is used to extract the Chinese text features, and then the two-way long and short-term memory network combined with the self-attention mechanism (BiLSTM - SelfAttention) is used to train the text features; based on the above operations, the self-attention mechanism, the multi-attention mechanism and the cross-attention mechanism combined with the BiLSTM and Transformer are used for the feature-level fusion and the hybridization of features, respectively. The three models, text, expression and audio, are fused together in a feature-level fusion amount and hybrid fusion, respectively. In this way, the models are able to learn the features of the three modalities, which in turn improves the ability to predict emotion categories. Experimental validation was carried out on the CH - SIMS public dataset, and the experimental results showed that the accuracy after expression, speech, text fusion, and multimodal fusion reached 86.08%, 83.61%, 91.29%, and 91.49%, respectively.

articleTitle: A wheel-track-leg composite unmanned ground platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In response to the limitations of existing unmanned ground platforms in terms of environmental adaptability, this paper proposes a type of unmanned ground platform with variable configuration, which integrates wheel-track transformation and wheel-leg switching, and has strong terrain adaptability. This article first introduces the overall plan of the unmanned ground platform and analyzes the subsystems. Then, dynamic analysis of the mechanism was conducted to obtain the foot trajectory and reachable space, and the swing inertia was also calculated. Finally, a co-simulation was conducted based on Simulink and ADAMS. The research results indicate that the unmanned ground platform has high feasibility and strong adaptability.

articleTitle: An Improvement of A Mobile RFID Authentication Protocol Based on Self-assembling Cross-bit Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Recently, Xu et al. proposed an ultra-lightweight mobile wireless two-way authentication protocol MAP-SKBO based on shared private keys and bit operations. This MAPSKBO is based on a bit operation scheme, using ultra-lightweight bit replacement and self-combination cross-bit operation to encrypt the transmitted information, and uses random numbers to maintain the freshness of the transmitted information and shared information private key. Xu et al. claimed that during the MAP-SKBO communication process, tags, readers, and databases can authenticate each other to resist attack destruction. However, this article will prove that their method has the disadvantage of leaking shared private keys, forging Tags, and Reader’s IDs.

articleTitle: Dynamic Correction and Deep Convolution-based Underwater Image Enhancement Algorithm for Underwater Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Addressing the issue of limited work efficiency for intelligent robots in extreme and complex underwater environments such as the seabed, we propose an innovative underwater image enhancement method that combines dynamic color correction and deep convolutional technology. Firstly, the classical Gray World color correction algorithm has been improved to more robustly handle the intricate color cast challenges in underwater environments. Following this, Dense Residual Blocks are introduced to deepen the architecture of the convolutional neural network. By incorporating fully connected layers, the transmission efficiency and accuracy of information within the network are enhanced. Additionally, we have designed a Parallel Attention Module that reduces the network's parameter burden while granting it flexible processing capabilities. Furthermore, a Global Compensation Module is proposed, which further boosts the network's adaptability to complex variations in underwater environments. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms relevant comparison algorithms in both subjective and objective tests, more effectively resolving underwater degraded images and enhancing the work efficiency of underwater robots.

articleTitle: Deep Spatio-Temporal 3D-Transformer Network for Traffic Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Accurate traffic flow prediction is increasingly vital for urban road planning and management. Recently, the existing models have made some progress in learning spatio-temporal features. However, they only focus on learning the dynamic spatio-temporal features from either local perspective or global perspective, while ignoring the comprehensive learning of correlations from both local and global perspectives, which limits their predictive performance. To this end, this paper proposes a Deep Spatio-Temporal Three-Dimentional Transformer Network (ST3DT-Net) for traffic flow prediction. Specifically, we first extract local dynamic spatio-temporal features via three-dimentional spatio-temporal decomposed convolutional blocks (3DSTDCB). Then, the global dynamic spatio-temporal features are learned based on three-dimentional vision Transformer (3D-Vit). The experiments are conducted on two typical traffic flow datasets. The results demonstrate the superiority of ST3DT-Net compared with the eight baselines.

articleTitle: Developing Cryptocurrency Trading Strategy Based on Autoencoder-CNN-GANs Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper leverages machine learning algorithms to forecast and analyze financial time series. The process begins with a denoising autoencoder to filter out random noise fluctuations from the main contract price data. Then, one-dimensional convolution reduces the dimensionality of the filtered data and extracts key information. The filtered and dimensionality-reduced price data is fed into a GANs network, and its output serve as input of a fully connected network. Through cross-validation, a model is trained to capture features that precede large price fluctuations. The model predicts the likelihood and direction of significant price changes in real-time price sequences, placing trades at moments of high prediction accuracy. Empirical results demonstrate that using autoencoders and convolution to filter and denoise financial data, combined with GANs, achieves a certain level of predictive performance, validating the capabilities of machine learning algorithms to discover underlying patterns in financial sequences.

articleTitle: Research on Substation Personnel Fall Detection Method Based on Vision-Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In power substation environments, ensuring personnel safety is critical to maintaining stable and reliable power operations. Detecting falls—a key safety concern—involves overcoming challenges such as low lighting, occlusion by equipment, and visually cluttered backgrounds. Conventional vision-only methods often fail to provide robust performance under these real-world conditions. In this work, we propose a novel fall detection approach leveraging large-scale pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs). By integrating textual semantics describing "fall" incidents with visual features from substation surveillance footage and performing incremental fine-tuning on domain-specific annotated datasets, our method achieves high-precision detection under challenging scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach surpasses traditional CNN-based methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and generalization. The findings offer a promising solution for intelligent safety monitoring and early warning systems in the power industry, reducing risks associated with personnel injuries and operational disruptions.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv11 Model for Detecting the Metal Roofing Tiles alongside the Railways
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Metal roofing tiles along railways pose significant hazards, potentially causing service disruptions and accidents. However, manual inspections are inefficient, limited in coverage, and lack automated data recording, rendering them insufficient to meet escalating safety requirements. This study introduces an enhanced YOLOv11-based intelligent detection method aimed at overcoming the challenges posed by complex backgrounds, occlusion, and real-time performance in the detection of metal roofing tiles along railway lines. The proposed method integrates attention modules, dynamic snake convolutions, and an enhanced loss function, achieving significant improvements in detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results on the railway dataset, comprising 5732 labeled images, demonstrate outstanding performance with mAP of 95.7%, while maintaining high detection speed and reliability.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of Capacitor Aging in MMC Based on Improved Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This article introduces a new fault detection method by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Gated Recursive Units (GRUs) for sub-module capacitors in Modular Multilevel Converters (MMCs). Considering the aging fault characteristics of these capacitors, the proposed method extracts feature from the sub-module capacitor voltages and their associated differential voltage waveforms, which are used as inputs to the proposed model. To improve the selection of hyper-parameters of the CNN-GRU neural network, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is utilized, then the aging condition of sub-module capacitors can be evaluated. Simulation results show that the proposed method is valid in monitoring capacitor aging in the MMC sub-module, with an overall accuracy of more than 98.2% in detecting and identifying capacitor aging.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction for Optical Network Based on Hybrid Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Optical networks are the cornerstone of the modern information society, serving as the backbone of global information transmission. The consequences of their failure would be significant, resulting in substantial losses. As the complexity and scale of optical networks continue to increase, the maintenance and fault-detection become increasingly challenging. Therefore this paper propose a fault prediction model based on CNN-LSTM-Attention: Firstly, the alarm log is preprocessed, and a sliding time window is employed to convert it into a standard input format for neural networks. Subsequently, the features are extracted through the CNN layer, and their forward and backward temporal relationships are learned through the LSTM layer and the Attention layer. Finally, the output prediction results are generated through the fully connected layer. To validate the efficiency of the proposed approach, a real dataset was employed for evaluation. To demonstrate the superiority of the CNN-LSTM-Attention model, its fault prediction outcomes were compared with CNN and CNN-LSTM. The results demonstrate that the CNN-LSTM-Attention model significantly outperforms the other two models in predicting faults in optical networks.

articleTitle: Addressing LLM Challenges: A Hybrid Framework for Duplicate Question Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Detecting similar or duplicate texts or questions is a critical subtask in information retrieval. Despite the remarkable advancements achieved by large language models (LLMs) in the question answering (QA) domain in recent years, challenges such as unreliable responses caused by LLM hallucinations and outdated information have highlighted the continued importance of information retrieval techniques. The integration of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with LLMs has mitigated some of these limitations, enhancing the reliability of applying LLMs to domain-specific knowledge. This paper uses Chinese educational questions as a case study and introduces an innovative framework for duplicate question detection, termed the Balanced Duplicate Question Detector (BDQD). The BDQD incorporates multiple extensible detectors and a machine learning-based balancer. Experimental results reveal that detecting duplicate questions involves an inherent trade-off between precision and recall. Logistic regression proves effective in balancing thresholds across different detectors, establishing a more stable and reliable standard for duplicate question determination. Finally, we propose a hybrid QA framework that considers both cost and efficiency, integrating the lightweight question retrieval architecture developed in this study with RAG and LLMs. This framework offers practical recommendations for building robust and efficient QA systems.

articleTitle: Research on an Information Encoding Technology for Representing Complex Tensor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This article addresses the characteristics of high-dimensional knowledge graphs, such as large node quantities, high attribute dimensions, numerous relationship types, and changes over time. It constructs entity relationship attributes by studying the multidimensional similarity between massive network target data and entity target data. A tensor model is used for the unified representation of high-dimensional knowledge graph data, resulting in a target relationship tensor model construction process. A tensor model for target similarity relations, which contains multidimensional information and refined structure, is established. The high-dimensional heterogeneous networks are transformed into relationship matrices to achieve knowledge conversion and unified expression modeling. This supports the unified representation of knowledge graphs for unstructured, semi-structured, and structured data, providing support for the engineering application of unified representations of high-dimensional knowledge graphs. This article employs the Tucker decomposition method to achieve low-dimensional representations of high-dimensional vectors and provides a detailed analysis of the decomposition process and algorithm. Experiments show that a three-dimensional tensor can be decomposed into two-dimensional factor matrices, achieving a unified representation of complex tensor information.

articleTitle: DOA-mono: Monocular Depth Estimation Focused On Dynamic Object Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Monocular depth estimation, as a fundamental task in the field of computer vision, has demonstrated significant application potential in areas such as autonomous driving and virtual reality (VR). Dynamic object perception refers to the model's ability to identify, locate, and effectively process the depth information of moving objects within a scene. Existing methods have shown excellent results in static scenes; however, when dealing with scenes containing moving objects, the rigid scene assumption is often violated due to the potential movement of fixed reference points in the scene. Existing methods lack the ability to perceive dynamic objects, resulting in reduced accuracy and low stability in depth estimation. To address the challenges posed by motion blur and dynamic scene changes caused by moving objects in monocular depth estimation, this paper proposes a monocular depth estimation network based on dense attention skip connections and a multi-scale feature fusion module. The proposed network enhances the model's dynamic object perception capability, improving depth estimation accuracy and robustness in complex dynamic scenes.

articleTitle: A Study on Miao Batik Pattern Design Based on Style Transfer Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to protect and conserve the Miao batik, a form of intangible cultural heritage, and to stimulate the creative evolution of its traditional patterns.It investigates the use of artificial intelligence technologies for the digital preservation and creative redesign of Miao batik patterns. Through the extraction and analysis of pattern elements, alongside the application of convolutional neural networks and style transfer algorithms, the research reimagines the features and aesthetics of these traditional patterns. The findings demonstrate that this approach not only supports the self-renewal and enhancement of the cultural value of Miao batik but also paves the way for its innovative evolution in a contemporary context.

articleTitle: Leveraging AIGC and Human-Computer Interaction Design to Enhance Efficiency and Quality in E-commerce Content Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In light of the accelerated growth of e-commerce, the generation of high-quality and efficient content has emerged as a pivotal factor in enhancing user experience and business value. However, conventional methods of content creation are prone to inefficiencies and creative constraints. This paper puts forth a comprehensive model based on the combination of existing generative pre-trained models and human-computer interaction design, with the objective of enhancing the efficiency and quality of e-commerce content generation. In particular, the initial stage of the process involves the utilisation of multi-modal data fusion technology, which facilitates the integration of diverse input sources, including images, videos, and textual data. This approach enhances the model's capacity to comprehend the multifaceted nature of products and services, thereby optimising the generation process. Secondly, a cross-domain sentiment analysis and recommendation engine was designed, which combined the self-attention mechanism in deep learning with the objective of analysing the popularity of the generated content according to consumer behaviour in real time and adjusting the generation strategy. Furthermore, the real-time feedback loop mechanism has been innovatively introduced, which enables the dynamic optimisation of content generation in accordance with user evaluation and click-through rate.
