This facilitates an improvement in the personalisation and accuracy of content. The experimental results demonstrate that the model markedly enhances the efficiency of content generation and user satisfaction on the e-commerce platform.

articleTitle: Design of License Plate Recognition System Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In order to detect the character information of license plate in image quickly and conveniently, this paper designs a license plate recognition system based on image processing. The image processing operation in this system is based on the association function in OpenCV libraries. Firstly, the image is denoised by image preprocessing and morphological transformation, and then the license plate is located by contour search and filtering. Then, the extracted license plate continues to perform image processing to segment each character in the license plate. Finally, the convolutional neural network is used to train the model to recognize each character. The experimental results show that the system has good timeliness and recognition effect.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Non-Invasive Intoxication Detection: Ocular Analysis of Drivers Using CNNs and Quanvolutional Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Current intoxication methods, though effective, often rely on intrusive procedures that require trained personnel or direct interaction with the individual, limiting their practicality for real-time applications [1], [2]. This study analyzes non-invasive approaches utilizing two Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and a Quanvolutional Neural Network (QNN) trained on eye images to classify sobriety by analyzing visual cues such as pupil dilation, eye redness, and eyelid position. All models were trained and evaluated on a dataset of 1500 labeled images, achieving accuracies ranging from 68.65% to 99.74%.

articleTitle: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning Algorithm for Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Path planning using the traditional RRT* algorithm in complex hospital environments has the drawbacks of not being able to avoid dynamic obstacles, too many redundant points, inefficient search and non-smooth paths, for this reason, this paper proposes an improved RRT* algorithm path planning method for medical delivery robots. The gravitational potential field and PRRT algorithm are introduced to optimize the sampling strategy, the adaptive step size is used to improve the search efficiency of the algorithm, and finally, the smoothness of the path is improved by branch pruning. Through simulation, the improved RRT* algorithm reduces the path turn point by 75%, the path length by 26.25%, and the search time by 89.72% compared to the traditional RRT* algorithm.

articleTitle: Curriculum-enhanced GroupDRO: Challenging the Norm of Avoiding Curriculum Learning in Subpopulation Shift Setups
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In subpopulation shift scenarios, a Curriculum Learning (CL) approach would only serve to imprint the model weights, early on, with the easily learnable spurious correlations featured. To the best of our knowledge, none of the current state-of-the-art subpopulation shift approaches employ any kind of curriculum. To overcome this, we design a CL approach aimed at initializing the model weights in an unbiased vantage point in the hypothesis space which sabotages easy convergence towards biased hypotheses during the final optimization based on the entirety of the available data. We hereby propose a Curriculum-enhanced Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (CeGDRO) approach, which prioritizes the hardest bias-confirming samples and the easiest bias-conflicting samples, leveraging GroupDRO to balance the initial discrepancy in terms of difficulty. We benchmark our proposed method against the most popular subpopulation shift datasets, showing an increase over the state-of-the-art results across all scenarios, up to 6.2% on Waterbirds and 2.9% on CivilComments.

articleTitle: Research on Minecraft Image Generation Method Based on Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Generative models have shown great potential in game image generation, especially for pixel-style games like Minecraft, where automatic content generation can significantly enhance the player experience. This paper investigates the application effects of unconditional DDPM, conditional DDPM, classifier-free DDPM, and guided DDPM in Minecraft image generation based on the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM). First, we trained an unconditional DDPM using over 3,000 images extracted from Minecraft videos to demonstrate its basic performance in terms of generation quality and detail retention. Subsequently, through comparative analysis, we found that classifier-free DDPM performed best in terms of detail richness and diversity, while guided DDPM was more suitable for generating consistent style content. Further evaluation of image generation effectiveness using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) indicates that classifier-free DDPM has a significant advantage in generation quality.

articleTitle: Research on User Upgrade and Replacement Prediction Algorithm Based on Improved LightGBM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In practical applications, the significance of accurately identifying potential car buyers far outweighs the risk of misclassifying non-buyers as potential buyers, thus the importance of the recall rate for positive samples. Consequently, this algorithm develops an enhanced incremental replacement prediction model designed to improve the recall rate of positive samples. Additionally, the algorithm introduces a novel approach for categorizing and labeling factors related to the age of replacement vehicles, thereby providing advanced data processing techniques and evaluation metrics to better describe the influence of various factors on the age of replacement vehicles. This methodology significantly enhances the accuracy of predicting the age of replacement vehicles.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Visual Odometry from RGB-D information
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel RGB-D multimodal fusion visual odometry (VO) method which is designed for challenging environments, including noisy, low-light, and variable lighting conditions. Existing methods which rely solely on RGB images perform badly under challenging conditions. To address this issue, our approach firstly employs a two-branch encoder to extract multimodal features. Then, a multi-head self-attention mechanism is utilized within two-branched encoder for highlighting informative information. Thirdly, we incorporates a dense bundle adjustment (DBA) module to optimize pose and depth estimation. Experiments on the TUM and TartanAir datasets show that the proposed method outperforms existing VO methods, such as REVO, ORBVO and TartanVO, making it highly suitable for applications in robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Steel surface defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Steel surface defect detection is an important step to ensure the quality of steel production. Aiming at the problems such as low detection accuracy and insufficient feature extraction ability in steel surface defect detection, an improved YOLOv8n steel defect detection algorithm FCV-YOLO was proposed. Firstly, the fast feature extraction module Faster-C2f replaces C2f in the backbone extraction network to enhance the feature extraction capability of the model. Secondly, the coordinate attention mechanism is introduced to improve the model's attention to important features. Finally, the parameter number and computation amount of the model are reduced through feature compression and simplification in the Neck structure, so that the model is more suitable for industrial scenarios with limited resources. Experiments on NEU-DET data set show that the average detection accuracy of the improved FCV-YOLO model is 77.6%, which can better meet the needs of steel surface defect detection.

articleTitle: Structural design and analysis of a novel ankle joint rehabilitation robot based on parallel mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems such as insufficient rehabilitation treatment and delayed treatment in the late stage of ankle sports injury. In this paper, a novel ankle rehabilitation robot based on parallel mechanism is proposed to provide effective rehabilitation training for patients with ankle sports injuries. Through the analysis of the motion mechanism of the ankle joint, the motion space requirement of the ankle joint rehabilitation robot is defined. Therefore, this paper designs a new ankle joint rehabilitation robot based on parallel mechanism which can realize dorsiflexion/plantar flexion, varus/valgus rehabilitation movement. The mathematical model of the structure is established by spiral theory, and the degree of freedom and kinematic constraint parameters of the system are determined. On this basis, three-dimensional software is used to optimize the structure design. In order to verify the rationality of the design of the mechanism, this paper uses simulation software to conduct dynamic simulation analysis of dorsiflexion/plantar flexion and inversion/valgus of the rehabilitation robot. The results show that the mechanism can stably perform the movement space requirements of rehabilitation and meet the expected Angle and displacement requirements. This design provides a new design direction for ankle joint rehabilitation robot.

articleTitle: Cement concrete pavement distress detection based on sensor fusion architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This study develops a cement pavement distress detection system based on a parallel fusion architecture. The algorithm of IMU includes two modified roughness indexes. The image subsystem uses the YOLOv7 network to detect four types of distress objects (e.g. longitudinal crack, transverse crack, complex crack, and pothole). The proposed system is evaluated in two types of cement pavement: urban and country. The experimental results validate the average detection rate of the sensor fusion reaches 90%. The proposed fusion strategy can compensate for any single-sensor failure and improve the detection accuracy of YOLOv7.

articleTitle: SE-DQN: local path planning method of mobile robots based on security exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: As a classical deep reinforcement learning method, Deep Q-Network (DQN) is widely used in path planning of mobile robots. However, in the complex unknown environments, due to lacking the guidance of prior knowledge and seeking the optimal path at the cost of frequent trial and error, DQN-based path planning methods have the problems such as difficult model convergence, low exploration efficiency and poor real-time obstacle avoidance ability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new path planning method named security exploration DQN (SE-DQN). In SE-DQN, the developed “expert experience” module combined with security exploration strategy guides the action selection to achieve collision-free safe exploration and improve exploration efficiency. In addition, an intensive reward function is meticulously designed so that the agent get timely feedback from the environment after performing each action. To verify SE-DQN’s performance, the convergence, generalization, and obstacle avoidance tests are designed and conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SE-DQN algorithm exhibits excellent convergence performance, environmental adaptability, and obstacle avoidance capabilities.

articleTitle: Effects of Dispersion and Phase Noise on QPSK and QAM System: Performance and Compensation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of dispersion and phase noise on quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) and quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) systems, as well as their compensation techniques, which are two fundamental modulation schemes widely used in digital communication. The motivation for this study is the growing demand for high-speed and reliable data transmission, which requires a deeper understanding of the impact of these damages on system performance. Through computer simulation, this work aims to gain a deeper understanding of the performance degradation caused by dispersion and phase noise, and to explore compensation techniques that can mitigate their adverse effects. We have discovered the impact of AWGN, dispersion, and phase noise on signal transmission and their manifestation on constellation diagrams. At the same time, compensation technology was used to compensate for dispersion and phase noise, which to some extent restored the distorted signal. Meanwhile, the BER-SNR curves of fibers with different linewidths under the influence of AWGN, dispersion, and phase noise were also explored to determine how to improve the bit error rate, enhance system performance, and achieve optimal communication performance of fibers.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification under PDE-based Cross-sensor Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The application of deep neural networks in image classification often demands a substantial amount of supervised data for training to yield relatively satisfactory outcomes. However, in the task of hyperspectral image classification, given the highly specialized nature of data annotation, the existing datasets are predominantly small-sized. The dearth of a large quantity of labeled image datasets for training poses a challenge in enhancing performance. Transfer learning mitigates the requirement for effective training with large-scale labeled samples by reusing the parameters of trained models and adapting them to related new tasks. Nevertheless, from the perspective of application scenarios, the characteristic that a single type of sensor only serves a specific region at a specific time results in the extraction of only one type of feature, which performs suboptimally on diverse datasets. Hence, the research on cross-sensor transfer learning is extremely pressing. Currently, the research on cross-sensor transfer learning mainly centers on extracting consistent features through more efficient models, yet this gives rise to the issue of an excessive number of parameters. PDE enhances the model generalization ability in cross-sensor hyperspectral image classification transfer learning through its stronger capacity for extracting consistent features, significantly reducing the number of parameters.

articleTitle: Automated Task Allocation for Multi-Drone Reconnaissance Missions Based on Optimized Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the mission environment, the cooperative execution of tasks by multiple UAVs has become an inevitable trend. This paper focuses on the automatic allocation of reconnaissance tasks for multiple UAVs and proposes an optimized discrete particle swarm algorithm. Firstly, the process of collaborative task instruction requests is optimized to reduce the response time. Then, an automated task allocation model with various constraints and performance functions is constructed. Subsequently, the model is solved based on the optimized discrete particle swarm algorithm. Through comparative experiments with other common methods, the results show that this algorithm performs well in terms of task allocation efficiency, the optimal value of the objective function, and execution time. It effectively improves the automatic task allocation ability of multiple UAVs in reconnaissance tasks and provides a strong guarantee for their cooperative operations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Dynamic Path Planning and Optimization for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the contemporary research context, path planning for autonomous vehicles in dynamic and uncertain environments represents a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose a dynamic path planning and optimisation framework for autonomous vehicles based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). This framework innovatively introduces real-time adaptability and an optimal path selection mechanism. The proposed model is based on DRL, with the addition of a convolutional neural network (CNN) and an attention mechanism to optimise the perception and decision-making process. In the context of path planning, CNNs facilitate the extraction of intricate features of the road environment, while the attention mechanism assists the model in prioritising critical environmental factors (e.g., traffic signals, obstacles, etc.), thereby enhancing the precision and efficiency of decision-making processes. Furthermore, the incorporation of reinforcement learning-based online learning capabilities enables the model to make adaptive adjustments according to real-time traffic conditions and dynamically plan the optimal path. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior performance in comparison to traditional path planning algorithms within a simulation environment, with an estimated enhancement in path planning efficiency of approximately 15%.

articleTitle: Root Cause Analysis Framework for Intelligent Computing Center
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The rapid development of AI technology has greatly increased the demand for computational power, leading many companies to deploy large-scale intelligent computing centers. However, the larger cluster sizes result in more frequent failures, making root cause analysis more challenging. To address these issues, we propose ASeqRCA, a novel framework for root cause analysis in intelligent computing center. We simplify the complex network structure of intelligent computing clusters and model the relationships between alarms in sequences by frequent-pattern mining and causal learning techniques. With an alarm causal graph, we apply depth-first search to identify potential alarm propagation paths. We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method through a real-world AI model training failure case.

articleTitle: ConsistencyPure: Consistency Models for Realtime Adversarial Purification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Diffusion-Based Purification (DBP) is a stochasticity-based defense method that effectively mitigates adversarial attacks but suffers from high computational costs due to its iterative reverse process. To address this, we propose ConsistencyPure, a novel purification framework leveraging a pre-trained consistency model distilled from diffusion models. ConsistencyPure requires only one forward and one reverse sampling step, achieving real-time purification while maintaining comparable defense performance and improving efficiency by one to two orders of magnitude. Our finding further confirms that the robustness of DBP stems primarily from randomness, independent of the diffusion framework’s iterative operations or noise prediction. Importantly, we highlight for the first time the crucial role of model representation learning in stochasticity- based defense methods. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness and practicality of ConsistencyPure.

articleTitle: Aircraft sheet metal riveting practical training safety protection detection algorithm based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the field of aircraft sheet metal riveting practical training safety and protection monitoring, it is crucial to accurately detect whether students are wearing goggles and noise-proof headphones. In this study, a dataset containing 4650 images was constructed for training and evaluating a YOLOv5-based target detection model. The YOLOv5 network structure is improved by optimizing the YOLOv5 network structure, replacing the backbone feature extraction network with PLCNet, using CNeB module for the Neck layer, and replacing GSConv with ordinary convolution. The experimental results show that the full-category mAP is significantly increased from 85.3% to 91.5%, which effectively enhances the model's ability to detect students' wearing of protective equipment in practical training, provides powerful technical support for improving the safety management level of aircraft sheet metal riveting practical training, and helps to create an intelligent and efficient safety monitoring system for aircraft maintenance practical training.

articleTitle: ComSAC: Multi-agent unmanned aerial vehicle swarm communication collaboration algorithm based on Soft Actor-Critic
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-agent communication and coordination framework for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms based on the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm. The proposed framework incorporates a master-slave communication model that effectively addresses challenges such as non-stationarity, partial observability, and high learning complexity in multi-agent systems. Experimental results in the simulation environment show that, compared to existing multi-agent methods, the proposed framework significantly enhances UAV task efficiency and communication coverage. Specifically, the communication coverage increased by 74.35%, the target search time was reduced by 57.04%, and the rate of redundant searches decreased by 23.21%. Particularly in complex environments and multi-target tasks, the proposed framework demonstrates exceptional stability and adaptability, providing a novel solution for efficient collaboration of UAV swarms in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Research on mobile intelligent terminal using Beidou satellite positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The country attaches great importance to the industrial application of Beidou. Promoting the quality improvement of satellite positioning, especially Beidou Positioning in mobile intelligent terminals, is an urgent need to promote the high-quality development of Beidou industry. This paper aims to promote the large-scale application of Beidou. It mainly studies whether the mobile terminal actually uses Beidou satellite in the process of positioning and the participation of Beidou satellite in positioning in detail. It uses the laboratory GNSS test system to carry out the cold and hot start first positioning test and dynamic positioning test on eight mobile intelligent terminals. It determines the actual use of Beidou satellite in terminal positioning by analyzing the positioning log of the terminal. It calculates the position of the terminal and the position of the simulated satellite by the simulator to obtain the positioning error of the terminal. It tests and analyzes the positioning error from the aspects of satellite search, first positioning and tracking positioning. Finally, it summarizes and plans to improve the positioning performance of Beidou terminal and Beidou application in the future.

articleTitle: Vibration Characteristic analysis of the structure of an intelligent bricklaying robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: An intelligent wall building robot is designed, which can realize the accurate positioning of the bricks in the wall building operation through the visual recognition system. The mechanical structure of the intelligent wall building robot is studied, and the structural vibration characteristics of the key components are analyzed, so that the whole mechanism can run stably in the working process. The wall building robot is mainly composed of steering chassis, lifting mechanism, manipulator mechanism, mortar supply mechanism, brick storage mechanism and visual recognition system. The skewer is the core conveying equipment in the mortar supply mechanism, the stable operation of skewer is directly related to the conveying efficiency of mortar. ANSYS Workbench is very important for the modal analysis of the sling structure. The first six frequencies and the frequency of the drive motor can be compared and analyzed to determine whether the sling mechanism has resonance with the drive motor, prevent resonance, prevent deformation and cracking of the mechanism, reduce noise, and improve the stability of the sling structure. The results show that the vibration characteristics of the mechanism can be analyzed by analyzing the mode of the mechanism and studying the natural frequency and displacement of the mechanism. Through the displacement diagram of the modal analysis, the parts of the mechanism with large displacement can be found out, and these parts are judged to be prone to deformation. The size of these parts can be adjusted, the mechanism can be reasonably optimized, and the stiffness of the skein mechanism can be improved. The stable operation of the wall-building robot is ensured.

articleTitle: Study on the motion design and control algorithm of humanoid robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The research on gait and action design of humanoid robot is the key point of humanoid robot research. Based on the research on motion stability criterion and trajectory planning of humanoid robot, this paper designs the action controller of humanoid robot and designs the corresponding control algorithm. With the help of the shr-6s humanoid robot, the motion and algorithm of the design were tested, and the motion design and control algorithm were proved to be feasible.

articleTitle: GeneA-SLAM: Enhancing SLAM with Genetic Algorithm-Based Feature Points Re-sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The uneven distribution of feature points significantly affects the performance of SLAM systems based on feature point matching. In this paper, a novel feature point resampling module based on genetic algorithm is proposed to alleviate the problem of feature point clustering. By integrating this module into the visual front end with the highly scalable ORB- SLAM2 as the global SLAM solution, GeneA-SLAM is developed. Experimental results on the TUM dataset reveal that, compared to ORB-SLAM2, GeneA-SLAM attains a maximum optimization of 19.73% in APE and 18.43% in RPE when taking translational components into account. Considering the rotational component, the maximum optimization rate of RPE reaches 50.10%. Moreover, GeneA-SLAM has a relatively lower runtime than ORB-SLAM2. Furthermore, GeneA-SLAM successfully accomplishes localization and constructs the environmental map on the sculpture dataset taken in a real environment. Overall, experiments confirm that GeneA-SLAM exhibits high accuracy and robustness. The GeneA-SLAM is available at https://github.com/qingshufan/GeneA-SLAM.

articleTitle: Novel Approach for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in Electromechanical Drive Systems Using an Attention-Based Residual 1D Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Numerous existing deep learning-based fault diagnosis models, have been implemented for intelligent fault diagnosis in electromechanical drive systems (EMDS). However, these models often are designed to detect and diagnose single fault types at specific operating conditions. These models are frequently susceptible to overfitting, suffer from the vanishing gradient problem, and struggle with long-range feature dependencies. Such limitations significantly hinder their accuracy and reliability in diagnosing complex fault scenarios for EMDS under different operating conditions using noisy data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel deep learning-based fault diagnosis model named Attention-based Residual 1D Convolutional Neural Network (AR1D-CNN). This model is designed to effectively diagnose complex faults in EMDS across various load conditions using noisy and imbalanced vibration data. Experimental results demonstrate exceptional classification accuracies of 99.98% and 100.00% on the KAIST dataset for 0 and 2 Nm load conditions, respectively, and 99.31% on the AETWPSU broken rotor bar dataset. Notably, the AR1D-CNN outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by approximately 4% on the AETWPSU dataset, highlighting its robustness and reliability. This research significantly enhances predictive maintenance strategies by enabling early and precise fault detection, ultimately improving the operational efficiency of EMDS.

articleTitle: Distributed Differential Privacy for Federated Learning: A Privacy-Enhancing Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To enhance data protection during federated learning training, this paper proposes a federated learning approach based on distributed differential privacy. In the distributed framework, a secure shuffle model is adopted as a trusted aggregator, and the shuffler randomly mixes reports and forwards them to the server for final analysis. In addition, the concept of Renyi divergence is introduced to more precisely control privacy loss. The results show that this method not only provides effective privacy protection for the federated learning training process, but also maintains good model performance, especially on the MINIST dataset.

articleTitle: Deployment Method of Emergency Communication Hub Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: An emergency communication hub contains multiple communication elements. The deployment locations of elements directly determine the communication efficiency of the entire hub. However, manual deployment often requires additional knowledge and longer planning time. This often results in commanders being unable to plan a high-quality deployment scheme immediately. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new algorithm based on deep Q-learning, which uses a fully convolutional network as its value network and is trained with the data accumulated in the example replay buffer. Compared to manual method, the experimental results show that the proposed approach can accomplish the task better and improve the deployment efficiency significantly.

articleTitle: Experimental system of active-passive integrated vibration isolation for robot with weak rigid support
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the manufacturing and assembly process of domestic large airplanes, the vibration in the surrounding environment greatly affects the working efficiency and precision of automated equipment. According to the vibration characteristics of the cabin environment, a multi-degree-of-freedom vibration isolation platform mechanism of robotics with weak rigid support applied in the cabin section of the aircraft is proposed, an experimental platform for the vibration isolation capability of a single outrigger is constructed, and a finite element analysis is carried out on the fixed frame of this experimental platform to verify its reliability.

articleTitle: MDT-YOLOv8s: Enhanced YOLOv8s model for X-ray contraband detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the challenges in X-ray security inspection, such as complex backgrounds, high rates of missed and false detections, severe occlusions, and scale variations, this paper proposes an improved detection model based on YOLOv8s, named MDT-YOLOv8s, to enhance detection accuracy. First, a multi-head self-attention mechanism is added to the final layer of the backbone network to improve feature extraction. Second, a Dynamic Head module is introduced to enhance the network's scale, spatial, and multi-task awareness, significantly improving detection performance. Finally, a Trapezoid loss function is designed to increase the relative loss of hard classified samples by assigning higher weights near the threshold μ, thus focusing attention on the optimization of difficult classified and error-prone samples. Experimental results on the SIXray dataset show that MDT-YOLOv8s improves the mean average precision (mAP) by 2.3% compared to the original YOLOv8s. The proposed model enhances detection capability and provides effective support for real-time security inspection applications.

articleTitle: Gaussian Process Regression-Based Wheel-Legged Robot Contact Force Estimation With PVDF Piezoelectric Film sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Wheel-legged robots combine the advantages of both wheeled and legged locomotion, enabling them to maintain balance, navigate, and perform stable tasks across complex terrains. This paper proposes an innovative method for contact force estimation in wheel-legged robots, utilizing PVDF (Polyvinylidene Fluoride) piezoelectric film sensors and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). The PVDF sensors are embedded in the inner surface of the foot-end tire, where they effectively detect dynamic changes in pressure and strain. The GPR model is employed to capture the complex nonlinear relationship between sensor readings and the contact forces along the three axes (Fx, Fy, Fz). The experimental setup includes a custom testing platform with a six-axis force sensor to measure actual contact forces, while the PVDF sensors provide force estimates. Results show that the GPR-based model offers high accuracy in estimating contact forces, with normalized root mean square errors (NRMSE) of 11%, 15%, and 16% for the Fx, Fy, and Fz axes, respectively. This sensor-based approach is lightweight, easy to install, and highly sensitive, making it a promising solution for contact detection in complex robotic systems and terrain classification tasks.

articleTitle: An Efficient Universal Information Extraction Framework for Bid Evaluation Experts Based on Attribute-relationship
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Expert information extraction (EIE) system is an automated information extraction framework designed to achieve efficient management and precise retrieval of expert resources in specific fields, whose accuracy is crucial to ensure the fairness of professional evaluation. In this research, an intelligent expert extraction system based on universal information extraction (UIE) is proposed to address the problems of high subjectivity and inefficiency of traditional manual expert extraction systems in dealing with large-scale data. Our framework uses ERNIE 3.0 as a pre-training model, and through the few-shot learning method, accurately extracts the attributes and relationships of expert information based on UIE. Thus, our system can quickly adapt and optimize the model under limited data conditions, significantly improving expert extraction’s accuracy and efficiency. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments have been conducted for our proposed framework, which achieves a high accuracy of 0.949 under 5-shots in the expert extraction task, significantly exceeding the performance of existing methods. The results of this research not only improve the objectivity and efficiency of EIE but also provide sustainable development of an efficient and accurate expert extraction system solution for various fields.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Network Based Control Strategy for Tiltrotor UAV: Transition Phase Longitudinal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Tilt-rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle have gained significant attention for their ability to rapidly respond to complex environments and execute long-range missions. The control challenges during the transition flight phase are particularly complex, involving highly nonlinear dynamics and intricate coupling between propulsion systems and aerodynamic forces. This study focuses on addressing the longitudinal control problem of TUAVs during their transition from rotor to fixed-wing mode. A novel control strategy is proposed, integrating a comprehensive understanding of vehicle dynamics with an advanced controller design. Specifically, a state feedback controller is combined with a Radial Basis Function Neural Network to enable real-time adaptive estimation of lift forces, thereby enhancing altitude tracking precision. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller significantly improves altitude tracking performance during the transition phase, achieving an 89% reduction in tracking error compared to the traditional PID controller.

articleTitle: An Improved RRT* Algorithm Based on Collision Density Detection for Manipulator Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the limitations of the RRT* algorithm in three-dimensional path planning, including insufficient obstacle-overcoming ability, susceptibility to local optima, and low search efficiency, this paper proposes an improved algorithm. The proposed method combines a heuristic cost function with an adaptive adjustment mechanism, leveraging local collision density detection to dynamically adjust the gain factor k. This optimizes the distribution of sampling points, enabling efficient obstacle traversal, escaping from local optima, and improved planning speed while maintaining path quality. Simulation experiments were conducted to compare the performance of the RRT algorithm, standard RRT* algorithm, heuristic-enhanced RRT* algorithm, and the proposed algorithm in three different environments. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach accelerates convergence, significantly enhances obstacle-overcoming and local optima avoidance capabilities, and ensures stable path quality.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Beamforming for Multicell ISAC: A Chance Constrained Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Chance-constrained optimization provides a powerful framework for decision-making under uncertainty and finds wide applications in areas. Conventional chance-constrained optimization assumes the transmission of the entire dataset to a single server, which may result in privacy breaches. In this paper, we propose a federated chance-constrained optimization approach for robust beamforming for multi-cell integrated sensing and communication systems. The proposed robust beamforming technique aims to minimize the worst-case base station transmission power while satisfying the chance constraint of communication rate with channel state information uncertainty as well as beampattern gain constraint of sensing target. Comprehensive simulation studies have been conducted to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed method and to corroborate the theoretical claims.

articleTitle: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)-based Path Loss Prediction Modeling for LoRa Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) has become a key enabler for connecting large-scale devices. LoRa technology plays a pivotal role in IoT due to its excellent anti-interference ability and long-range transmission capabilities. However, environmental factors, terrain, and building occlusion significantly impact the propagation and loss of path of LoRa signals, which in turn affect network coverage and communication quality. Therefore, accurately predicting the path loss of LoRa signals is crucial for effective network optimization and troubleshooting. In this study, we propose a path loss prediction model based on a multilayer perceptron (MLP), integrating the Okumura model path loss as a reference feature and comparing it with traditional empirical models. The experimental results demonstrate that the MLP model effectively learns complex nonlinear relationships, improving the accuracy of prediction. Through 10-fold cross-validation and testing various neuron configurations, it is found that the MLP model with 20 neurons (MLP20) performs best, yielding the lowest root mean square error (RMSE). Compared to the traditional Okumura Hata model, the MLP model shows significant advantages in prediction accuracy and stability. This study not only takes advantage of the theoretical strengths of the Okumura model but also enhances the adaptability to complex environmental factors through MLP, providing a new solution for LoRa network optimization.

articleTitle: An Improved Potential Bi-Directional RRT Path Planning Method for Space Redundant Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: RRT-Connect method can be utilized to find feasible paths for space redundant robots when performing complex in-orbit operations. However, its reliance on random sampling without leveraging obstacle information often leads to the generation of numerous invalid nodes that collide with obstacles, thereby increasing computational costs. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Improved Potential Bi-Directional RRT (IPB-RRT) algorithm that integrates an enhanced potential field and a pre-sampling strategy. The improved potential field tackles the local minima problem by refining the repulsive force and incorporating an RRT-exchange mechanism based on tree structure information. The pre-sampling strategy gathers prior environmental information by identifying collision states in joint space before tree expansion begins, enabling more efficient pathfinding. Simulation results in both simple and complex environments demonstrate that the proposed IPB-RRT algorithm significantly outperforms RRT-Connect by achieving shorter planning times, greater obstacle distance, and a substantially reduced number of invalid nodes. These improvements enhance the safety and reliability of paths, making the algorithm suitable for space robots performing challenging tasks.

articleTitle: A local target enhanced reconnaissance algorithm based on autonomous exploration of robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This study proposes a new robot autonomous exploration algorithm that enhances local target reconnaissance, addressing the shortcomings of existing autonomous exploration methods in recognizing specific targets locally and conducting further reconnaissance. The algorithm consists of two key parts: global autonomous exploration and local target reconnaissance. The global autonomous exploration module is responsible for map construction and autonomous exploration. The local target reconnaissance module is responsible for detecting and identifying preset targets. When a target that requires reconnaissance tasks is identified, it plans and explores the order of task execution. The experimental results show that compared with traditional methods, this algorithm successfully completes the target surround reconnaissance task in specific local target reconnaissance tasks, while providing more comprehensive environmental exploration.

articleTitle: Research on robot automatic assembly system based on automatic programming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative automated robotic assembly system for intelligent manufacturing, designed to minimize setup time and costs by reducing the need for frequent task reassignments in robotic operations. The proposed system combines two core elements: robots learning assembly tasks through human demonstrations and embodying these learned tasks as robot skills. Initially, robots observe human assembly operations, which are formalized into human assembly scripts. These scripts are then converted into robot-specific assembly tasks through workspace modeling and action planning, supported by simulation redirection, enabling the execution of a range of tasks. The system equips robots with pre-trained skills, enabling them to autonomously perform complex tasks that involve inherent uncertainty and variability. To validate the approach, a prototype assembly system was developed for power circuit breakers and electronic set-top boxes. The experimental results confirm that the proposed system is not only feasible but also significantly reduces the need for human intervention in automated robotic assembly, highlighting its potential to optimize manufacturing processes. This approach offers a promising solution to enhance the efficiency, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness of robotic automation in production environments, making it suitable for a wide range of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Research on High-Precision Detection Scheme for Scenic Area Garbage Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the rapid development of tourism, the issue of garbage pollution in scenic areas has become increasingly severe. Traditional manual cleaning methods are inefficient and prone to omissions. To address this problem, this paper proposes a high-precision garbage detection scheme (EYOLO-G) based on an improved YOLO algorithm. By introducing a lightweight network structure (GhostNet and Slim-Neck), a Coordinate Attention mechanism (CA), and a multi-scale receptive field module (RFB), the proposed method effectively enhances the detection accuracy of small-object garbage and improves the real-time performance of the system while reducing the model's parameter count and computational complexity. Experimental results show that the EYOLO-G model achieves mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 scores of 96.20% and 77.77%, respectively, significantly outperforming mainstream object detection algorithms. This provides an efficient and intelligent solution for environmental management in smart scenic areas.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Emergency Monitoring Base Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Air pollution resulting from sudden atmospheric environmental incidents significantly impacts the economic development and public health in affected regions. Precise quantitative emergency monitoring and assessment are critical tasks for environmental authorities. Traditional emergency monitoring primarily relies on human labor; however, it is challenging for personnel to access hazardous core areas, such as the incident site. Consequently, manually collected data often lack timeliness, accuracy, and comprehensiveness. The tracked base robot is a pivotal element of the system, fulfilling an essential function. Designed as a versatile mobile platform, it boasts robust data processing and storage capabilities, enabling it to receive, integrate, and analyze extensive environmental data transmitted by the leg-wheel monitoring robots. Equipped with a heavy-duty track system, the base robot ensures reliable mobility across diverse and challenging terrains, maintaining operational efficiency even under adverse conditions. Furthermore, its integrated high-capacity batteries and charging infrastructure not only supply power to the leg-wheel monitoring robots but also serve as a secure hub for maintenance and data uploads, ensuring the sustained functionality and secure data transfer within the entire monitoring network.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 algorithm for student behavior detection in a smart classroom
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In light of the advancements in educational technology, the smart classroom has emerged as a pivotal element in the contemporary educational landscape. Among these, student behavior detection technology is of particular importance for enhancing the quality of teaching and facilitating students' personal growth. In order to address the shortcomings of limited public datasets and low detection precision, we have created the SBC Dataset and proposed a student behavior detection algorithm, CCB-YOLOv8, which builds upon the YOLOv8 framework. Firstly, Coordinate Attention mechanism is introduced in the YOLOv8 backbone network to enhance the model's spatial perception. Secondly, the original UpSample operator is replaced by the CARAFE operator to augment the model's ability to capture key features. Finally, we introduce BiFPN in the Concat module to improve the precision and generalisation ability of the system. In comparison to YOLOv8, the precision of CCB-YOLOv8 has been enhanced by 4.3%, the recall by 5.6%, and the mAP@0.50 and mAP@0.50:0.95 by 4.4% and 5.5%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the improved algorithm exhibits heightened accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Deploying While Exploring: A Greedy-based Communication Beacons Deployment in Multi-Vehicle Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In multi-vehicle collaborative exploration of unknown environments, it is still a great challenge to maintain the communication between multiple vehicles. In this paper, we present a greedy-based communication beacon deployment method to address this challenge. The proposed method involves each vehicle performing LiDAR-inertial odometry, hierarchical grid-based exploration, and greedy-based beacon deployment. Each time a vehicle reaching the communication boundary, beacon candidate positions are selected. A candidate location that can cover the most uncommunicated area is selected as beacon placement points. Through simulation experiments, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated, showing that it can dynamically deploy beacons to maintain communication within the explored area while minimizing the number of beacons used.

articleTitle: A Review of the development of Visual SLAM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Simulated Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology is one of the core technologies in the navigation field of autonomous mobile robots and unmanned aerial vehicles, which enables the machines to simultaneously locate themselves and build environmental maps through visual sensors (such as cameras). This technology has important applications in the fields of self-driving cars, augmented reality, and automatic navigation. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of visual SLAM, focusing on its theoretical basis, key technologies, and development in the past decades. This paper first summarizes the basic principle and classification of SLAM technology, and then deeply discusses the theoretical basis of visual SLAM, including image processing, computer vision, state estimation, and kinematics. Then, the paper introduces the development of key technologies of visual SLAM in detail. Finally, this paper discusses the application of visual SLAM in UAV navigation, robot exploration, and virtual reality, and points out the limitations of current technology and the future research direction, including multi-sensor fusion, deep learning application, real-time performance improvement and SLAM technology in antagonistic environment. The main contribution of this review is to sort out the latest progress of visual SLAM in detail and look forward to the future development trend and potential research direction.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Hybrid Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In response to the current issues with lower limb rehabilitation robots, a 3-degree-of-freedom hybrid lower limb exoskeleton has been designed. This exoskeleton consists of three parts: a waist device, a hip device, and a knee device. The waist structure can adaptively fit different body shapes. The hip device is a 3-UU mechanism that enables rehabilitation training for hip joint flexion/extension and adduction/abduction. The knee device is a URU-RRR parallel mechanism that facilitates rehabilitation training for knee joint flexion/extension. The modified Gruebler's formula was used to calculate the degrees of freedom of the mechanism, and the workspace cloud map of the mechanism was plotted using MATLAB. The driving function was input into Adams to obtain the end-effector motion trajectory. Finally, static analysis of key components was performed in Ansys Workbench to obtain the stress and deformation cloud maps of the mechanism.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Model for Scene Perception in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the support of autonomous driving technology, the development of electric vehicles has accelerated significantly in recent years. Computer vision plays a crucial role in scene perception and decision-making processes in autonomous driving systems. However, efficiently processing vision tasks like drivable area and lane line segmentation in real-time remains a major challenge in resource-constrained environments. To address this aspect, we present DriveLaneNet, a lightweight multi-task learning model optimized for such conditions. The model adopts MobileNetV3 as its backbone and integrates an efficient neck module to merge multi-scale semantic features. Additionally, we introduced an attention module that effectively enhances the model's understanding of global information, improving its performance in complex scenarios. Experiments reveal that DriveLaneNet achieves competitive results in drivable area and lane line segmentation tasks, requiring just 0.3M parameters. On an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 GPU, it delivers over 100 FPS. Although slightly trailing state-of-the-art (SOTA) models in accuracy, DriveLaneNet offers remarkable computational efficiency and real-time capability, making it ideal for embedded applications.

articleTitle: O2M: Online Opponent Modeling in Online General-Sum Matrix Games
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper focuses on strategy learning in online general-sum games, specifically addressing online matrix games (MGs), where two players control parameters and face an unknown, stochastically varying payoff matrix. The goal is to learn strategies that maximize long-term rewards within this dynamic and uncertain game environment. We introduce Online Opponent Modeling (O2M), a novel algorithm designed to overcome the limitations of OMG-RFTL, which struggles in general-sum game settings. O2M incorporates opponent modeling techniques into online game frameworks, alleviating the non-stationarity issue inherent in multi-agent systems and enabling agents to achieve superior rewards.

articleTitle: Adaptive Step-wise Bi-directional Evolutionary Structural Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In the process of structural optimization design for components, fixed step size in the Evolutionary Structural Optimization and Bi-directional Evolutionary Structural Optimization methods result in slow convergence speed and excessive element deletion. To resolve these issues, we propose an adaptive-step BESO method. It employs discrete performance indicators and control factors to dynamically adjust step sizes, aiming to minimize the harmonic response of nodal displacements. By accounting for variations in structural volume and element sensitivity, this method improves convergence rate and stability. The resulting topology meets volume constraints without empirical estimations or oscillations. Numerical examples confirm that the adaptive-step approach enhances computational efficiency, achieves progressive convergence in volume and harmonic response, and produces a clear, well-defined topology.

articleTitle: Spatial Temporal Period Transformer Networks for Traffic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: As a crucial component of intelligent transportation system, traffic forecasting still faces challenges in achieving timely and accurate results. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Spatial-Temporal Period Transformer Networks (STPTN) to improve the accuracy of traffic forecasting by incorporating both dynamic graph spatial dependencies and temporal periodic dependencies. We utilized Graph Attention Networks (GAT) and multi-head attention mechanism to simulate the real-world relations of traffic sequences and better extract their dependency from the static and dynamic perspectives, respectively. By extracting spatial and temporal dependencies in parallel, it not only enhances learning efficiency, but prevents interference between spatial and temporal dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate that STPTN has achieved state-of-the-art results in the accuracy of traffic forecasting compared to several existing methods.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Driving Style Classification Real-World Data Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Driving style remains a critical factor that influences traffic behavior and, hence, risks of accidents even when Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving technologies are increasingly available. In this study, a machine learning-based methodology is proposed for classifying driving into three categories: conservative, normal, and aggressive. Simulation data were used for training the model, although real-world data applications were given for a rigorous evaluation to ensure practical applicability. Several key features, such as acceleration, deceleration, lateral acceleration, throttle input, and brake usage, were analyzed for the classification. The Random Forest model, through comparative analysis, was selected based on better accuracy and generalization. A sliding window technique and statistical feature extraction were used to improve dataset diversity and learning on time-series data. It worked with an 86.7% accuracy rate on real-world data, which sheds light on its robustness for boosting driver behavior analysis as well as personalized driver-assistance technologies.

articleTitle: Question generation based on knowledge base
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Question generation refers to automatically generating reasonable and relevant questions based on given text and answers. The application prospects of question generation technology are very broad and it has become one of the research hotspots in the field of natural language processing. In knowledge-based question generation, most models only focus on the answer entity in the knowledge base and ignore other information related to the entity, while many models are not adaptable to out-of-vocabulary predicates. To address this shortcoming, this paper proposes a controlled generation framework based on a knowledge base, which controls the generator through constraints to ensure that the given answers and key entities in the subgraph appear in the generated questions. At the same time, an optimization strategy for the pre-trained generation model is proposed, which first adjusts the parameters in the decoder and then freezes the parameters in the encoder, so that the model can retain the characteristics of the hidden predicates in the pre-trained model, thereby improving the model's adaptability to out-of-vocabulary predicates and improving the quality of generated questions.

articleTitle: Corporate Carbon Emission Prediction Based on Multi-Source Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of corporate carbon emissions is imperative for investors, policymakers, and the global environmental agenda. Traditional methods, primarily leveraging structured data, often fail to capture the nuanced, influential factors pertinent to corporate emissions. This paper introduces a new pathway that integrates multi-source data to construct diverse machine learning models for enhanced prediction. We implemented a semi-supervised machine learning framework to analyze CSR reports from Chinese A-share companies, extracting textual features through a specially developed Corporate Green Action Index (CGAI). We conduct a comparative analysis of carbon emissions prediction using five machine learning models. The experimental results show that the fusion of numerical and textual data provides a new prediction accuracy and climate risk assessment model, and the prediction accuracy is significantly improved compared with traditional models.

articleTitle: Path planning of mobile robots based on obstacle motion prediction assisted by artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper conducts optimization research on the problem of local dynamic obstacle avoidance path planning for mobile robots. Based on the current historical position trajectory of dynamic obstacles, a dynamic obstacle motion trend prediction algorithm is proposed. In the process of dynamic obstacle avoidance path planning for mobile robots, considering the current position of obstacles, the movement trajectory of dynamic obstacles is evaluated. An improved D* Lite path planning algorithm is proposed, which greatly improves the efficiency and safety of the robot’s dynamic obstacle avoidance algorithm. A simulation verification environment is built, and typical single dynamic obstacle and multi-dynamic obstacle scenarios are given to compare and verify the effectiveness of the obstacle avoidance path planning algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi differential gear train AGV fine positioning system and control method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper provides a multi-differential gear train AGV precise positioning system and control method, which solves the problems of poor autonomous positioning accuracy and low efficiency of multi-differential gear train AGV. The test results show that the positioning system and control method have low cost, simple structure and high precision. The angle error is less than ± 1 °, the horizontal and vertical error is less than ± 1mm, and the adaptability is strong. The positioning accuracy can be set freely, which is worth popularizing in large area on the differential gear train AGV.

articleTitle: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on Meta-DQN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Currently, artificial intelligence shows vigorous development. Mobile robot path planning, as a fundamental research topic in the field of artificial intelligence, is constantly undergoing iterative upgrades every year. DQN, as a traditional algorithm for deep reinforcement learning, has many limitations: the training process is trial and error by interacting with the environment intermittently, but every time it finishes training, the model needs to start from scratch to train the next task, which results in low-quality samples, long training time, and poor robustness. To solve the above problems, this study adds meta-learning on the basis of the traditional DQN algorithm to form a meta-depth reinforcement learning improvement algorithm, which takes advantage of their strengths and complements their weaknesses, utilizes the ability of meta-learning to adapt to the new task quickly, and fine-tunes the model through meta-knowledge so that the model itself obtains an autonomous learning mechanism, which greatly reduces the time to train the model. The environment was set as a raster map, the starting point, end point, and roadblock were determined, and the simulation was carried out on the MATLAB platform. The results show that the improved algorithm possesses the advantages of reducing the frequency of interaction with the environment, arriving at the goal point smoothly, and taking a shorter time compared with the traditional DQN algorithm.

articleTitle: Reward Design Framework Based on Reward Components and Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the field of robotics has gained widespread attention. Due to their powerful code generation and contextual understanding capabilities, these models can generate reward functions from task commands, prompts, and environmental code, thus aiding robots in acquiring skills through reinforcement learning (RL). However, reward functions generated by existing models often suffer from issues of low executability and success rates, particularly when handling vague or complex task commands. These models usually require multiple iterations of optimization to achieve the desired outcomes. To address this challenge, we propose a reward function generation method based on reward components, which leverages human-level prior knowledge to improve generation efficiency and accuracy. Specifically, we have constructed a task→reward components dataset and fine-tuned a Reward Component Generator (RCG) using this dataset. The RCG then guides the automatic generation of reward functions for reinforcement learning tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly improves reward executability, accuracy, and task success rate compared to state-of-the-art approaches. For more information, please visit our project website at: https://jkx-yy.github.io/RCG/

articleTitle: U-shaped Dual Attention Transformer: An Efficient Transformer Based on Channel and Spatial Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Transformer-based methods have demonstrated remarkable performance on image super-resolution tasks. Due to high computational complexity, researchers have been working to achieve a balance between computation costs and performance. Restormer has achieved commendable balance by utilizing global channel attention. However, the performance is limited by insufficient local pixel reconstruction. In this paper, we propose a U-shaped Dual Attention Transformer (UDAT) with local-global receptive field, addressing the limitation of Restormer in local pixel reconstruction. We propose a dense window channel attention to enhance the local feature representation, more efficient in computational complexity. Experiments demonstrate that our UDAT achieve superior performance compared with Restormer on benchmark datasets, surpassing Restormer by 0.57 dB on the Urban100 dataset. On-par with SwinIR, our method reduces computational complexity by 3.2 times and improves inference speed by 2 times, achieving a better balance between computational costs and performance.

articleTitle: Path planning of mobile robot based on improved ant colony optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Path planning for mobile robots is a critical research area in intelligent control and automation. To address the issues of slow convergence and susceptibility to local optima in traditional ant colony algorithms within complex environments, this paper introduces a series of improvement strategies. An attenuation function is incorporated to optimize heuristic information, enabling ants to rely more on pheromone-based decision-making in the later stages. Directional guidance angles are added to enhance the directivity of state transition probabilities, accelerating the path search process. Additionally, cubic B-spline curves are employed to smooth the paths, while the 2-opt algorithm is integrated to further minimize path lengths. These enhancements significantly improve the algorithm's efficiency and stability. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in path planning performance, offering an effective solution for optimizing mobile robot navigation in complex environments.

articleTitle: Enhanced Genetic Algorithm for Traveling Salesman Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Aiming at the challenges faced by genetic algorithms in solving the traveler’s problem, including the low quality of initialized population, slow convergence speed, and the tendency to fall into local optimal solutions, this paper proposes an Enhanced Genetic Algorithm for Traveling Salesman Problem (EGAT). The algorithm has the following four key improvements: (1) Improved greedy heuristic to initialize the population: this study introduces an improved greedy heuristic to initialize the population, which not only improves the quality of the initial solution, but also accelerates the convergence speed of the global search. (2) Introducing tournament selection mechanism: we adopt a tournament selection mechanism, in which a number of individuals are randomly selected to compete in order to select the one with the highest fitness. Compared with the traditional roulette wheel selection, this method effectively maintains the diversity of the population and avoids the algorithm from converging to the local optimal solution too early. (3) Application of Partial Matching Crossover operator: when generating offspring, the use of Partial Matching Crossover operator can retain the order information of the original paths, which greatly improves the quality of offspring. This design not only ensures the generation of legitimate paths, but also enhances the diversity among the offspring, which helps to explore the solution space more comprehensively.(4) Combination of diversified mutation strategy and 2-opt local search: a diversified mutation strategy is designed, including swap mutation, insertion mutation and inversion mutation. These variants enhance the exploratory nature of the search process while maintaining appropriate variant probabilities. The combination of local search techniques further optimizes the path quality.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Digital Array Radar for UAV Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation process of a digital array radar system for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) monitoring. The digital section of the radar employs multiple FPGA boards, which operate in coordination to achieve radar waveform generation, echo signal acquisition, and data transmission functions. The paper first provides a detailed description of the overall radar system design, including the antenna and RF subsystems, intermediate frequency (IF) digital transceiver subsystem, data transmission subsystem, and signal processing modules. Subsequently, field experiments were conducted using the developed radar system. The collected echo data were used to evaluate the radar's UAV detection performance and elevation coverage range. The results demonstrated the system's performance indicators and the feasibility of the platform for UAV detection.

articleTitle: GHP-ManageFormer: A Transformer-Enhanced Approach for Logistics Transportation Time Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Transformer-based deep learning model, GHP-ManageFormer, for solving the problem of logistics and transportation timeliness prediction. The model adopts a multi-layer architecture, which processes static, temporal, and dynamic features in logistics and transportation through feature processing and attention layers. The core innovation of the model lies in the introduction of a spatiotemporal-aware multi-head attention mechanism and a cross-modal integration strategy to achieve effective fusion of multi-source heterogeneous data. Experiments based on a logistics dataset containing more than 100,000 delivery route records show that GHP-ManageFormer outperforms existing methods in terms of both the root mean square error (RMSE=1.240) and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.856), significantly improving the performance of the Transformer benchmark model. In addition, the model has the ability to estimate the uncertainty of the prediction results, providing more comprehensive reference information for practical logistics decisions.

articleTitle: AETSA: Adaptive Selection and Dynamic Diversity Enhancement of Evolutionary Tree Species Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Since the original TSA has problems such as easy to fall into local optimum and limited population diversity, this study proposes an optimized Tree-Seed Algorithm(TSA), which significantly improves the search efficiency and global optimization ability of the algorithm by introducing an adaptive selection mechanism(ST), dynamic step-size adjustment and population diversity enhancement strategy. The adaptive selection mechanism dynamically adjusts the search trend based on the changes of the current iteration number and the global optimum, effectively balancing the local search and global search. In addition, the algorithm further optimizes the balance between exploration and exploitation by dynamically adjusting the step size (d). The population diversity enhancement mechanism is fused by randomly selecting individuals, and this fusion strategy is based on the weighted differential variance of three random individuals, which helps the algorithm to jump out of the local optimal solution. Combining these innovations, the improved tree species algorithm (AETSA) solves the limitation problem of the original TSA. Experimental results show that AETSA outperforms benchmark algorithms such as TSA, EST-TSA, DE, BOA, and GA in terms of accuracy and convergence speed, and the algorithm in this study demonstrates excellent performance and adaptability in solving complex optimization problems.

articleTitle: NeuroMotion: A lightweight and Portable Rehabilitation Training System for Motor Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In response to the problems of poor portability and low decoding efficiency of the current rehabilitation system based on motor imagery(MI). In this paper, we propose a lightweight and portable MI-based rehabilitation training system named NeuroMotion, which consists of two parts: signal acquisition and signal decoding. Signal Acquisition: Only 8 channels are used to acquire MI EEG signals to improve the portability of the system. Signal decoding: A Triple-Branch Shallow Convolutional Neural Network (TBSCNN) model is constructed to achieve efficient decoding of EEG signals from motor imagery; branches 1 and 2 of the TBSCNN consist of one layer of temporal convolution and one layer of spatial convolution, while branch 3 consists of one layer of temporal-space fusion convolution. The three branches extract EEG spatio-temporal features in parallel and finally output the categories after one universal convolutional layer. Experimental results show that the NeuroMotion proposed in this paper improves the portability and decoding efficiency of the rehabilitation system. The signal decoding model TBSCNN achieves 84.37% MI EEG binary classification accuracy on the self-acquisition dataset. The lightweight EEG decoding model and the setup of a small number of EEG acquisition channels lay the foundation for the development of a low-power, portable brain-computer interface rehabilitation device.

articleTitle: Emergent Behavior in Spiking Neural Networks: A Study on Complex Network Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs), often referred to as the "third-generation" artificial neural networks, closely emulate the bio-inspired characteristics of global weakly supervised learning and local unsupervised bio-optimization.
