The neurons in SNNs more accurately mirror biological neurons. Increasing evidence suggests that biological neural networks exhibit complex network structures. To gain a deeper understanding of spiking neural networks, it is essential to focus on the organization and topology of their networks. In this paper, we construct several spiking neural network models with complex network structures and apply continuous external inputs to the target networks. By observing the emergent behavior of these models under different structural configurations, we analyze the influence of external inputs on networks with varying topologies. Our findings aim to provide a foundation for uncovering and harnessing the intelligent behaviors inherent in spiking neural networks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Vehicle Trajectory Planning via Combined Dynamic and Quadratic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by non-convex optimization in path planning for intelligent vehicles using numerical optimization techniques, this study introduces a combined approach leveraging dynamic programming (DP) and quadratic programming (QP). The dynamic programming algorithm is employed for path search, with the solution space defined by road and obstacle boundaries. Subsequently, a QP algorithm is applied to optimize the path represented by a quintic polynomial curve, effectively mitigating the no-solution issue commonly associated with non-convex optimization. Similarly, velocity planning follows a dual approach of dynamic programming and quadratic programming. The dynamic programming algorithm generates an initial velocity solution, incorporating vehicle dynamics constraints, and the QP algorithm is then used to refine the velocity profile. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed trajectory planning strategy in both static and dynamic scenarios.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Learning-Based Integrated Water Quality Assessment and Pollution Source Tracing Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In light of the mounting issue of water pollution, the precision and real-time capability of water quality monitoring have emerged as a pivotal subject in the domain of environmental conservation and public health. This paper presents a comprehensive water quality assessment and pollution source tracking model based on multi-task learning (MTL). On the basis of the existing water quality prediction and pollution source identification models, we propose a multi-task learning framework which jointly trains multiple related tasks. This framework is designed to enable the collaborative optimisation of water quality parameter assessment and pollution source tracking. In particular, we extend the traditional single-task model to jointly learn water quality indicators and pollution source characteristics through shared representations, and simultaneously carry out pollution source location prediction within the same framework. The model employs a multi-branch neural network architecture, wherein each branch is tasked with a distinct objective but interacts with information through a shared network layer, thereby facilitating knowledge transfer and enhancing the model's generalisation ability. Furthermore, a dynamic weighting mechanism is introduced to ensure a balanced contribution of each task and enhance the robustness of the model. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior performance in terms of water quality prediction accuracy and pollution source tracking efficiency compared to existing advanced technology.

articleTitle: Research on Gait Planning for Elderly Biomimetic Robot Dogs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This study conducts an in-depth exploration of the gait issues of bionic robotic dogs for elderly care. The main objective of this research is to improve the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm through deep learning technology to enhance the gait control capabilities of bionic robotic dogs. Specifically, we aim to address the limitations of traditional control methods when dealing with dynamic environments. enable robots to walk more naturally in complex scenarios and interact effectively with humans. To this end, we will explore the combination of deep learning and MPC algorithms, aiming to achieve greater flexibility and adaptability. A deep neural network is used for learning and predicting gait data, which is integrated with the MPC algorithm to adjust gait control strategies through real-time feedback. Through a large number of simulation experiments and practical tests, we have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method. The contribution of this research lies in the proposal of a deep learning-based MPC algorithm, which significantly enhances the gait control performance of bio-mimetic robotic dogs.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Control Strategy of Five-link Wheel-legged Robot Based on Model Predictive Control Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Compared with traditional wheeled or legged robots, wheeled legged robots can maintain better stability in unstable terrain, but nonlinear system control of wheeled legged robots in strongly disturbed terrain still faces challenges. This article proposes an integrated adaptive control strategy that integrates two control models based on the kinematic characteristics of a five link legged robot. Firstly, in order to streamline the complex overall motion model of the robot, the motion of the robot is decoupled into two parts: the body and the legs. Secondly, an MPC-LADRC (Model Predictive Control Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control) integrated adaptive control method is proposed, which uses LADRC to correct the MPC optimization problem and improve the stability of the wheeled legged robot in complex terrain. The simulation comparison verification results show that compared with the Anti-interference controller based on LQR (linear quadratic regulator), the MPC-LADRC controller has better control accuracy, speed tracking response, and anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Graph Network-Based Traffic Forecasting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Traffic forecasting is widely recognized as a fundamental component of smart city development; however, classic models struggle to manage long-term time series data effectively. In other words, existing models rely on multiple algorithm modules, which significantly increase computational costs and, in turn, reduce model accuracy. Furthermore, any new input dataset requires retraining the model from scratch. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel approach, where a long-sequence embedding module and an encoder-decoder structure integrating a temporal attention layer and a graph convolution operator are introduced during the pretraining section. In the fine-tuning section, the learned parameters are frozen, and the decoder is replaced with a prediction header that incorporates a meta-learning module. This approach enables the integration of both long-term and short-term time series data while facilitating training tailored to specific target tasks. The method has demonstrated strong performance on real-world datasets, providing clear evidence of its effectiveness in addressing traffic forecasting challenges.

articleTitle: Multilevel Attention-based Multimodal Emotion Recognition from Text and Audio
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Automatic emotion recognition has been a longstanding challenge in the field of affective computing. Within this domain, Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has gained increasing attention as a promising application of machine learning. The primary objective of SER is to enhance emotion detection by leveraging specific types of features (such as MFCC and spectral features) or by combining multiple feature types. However, current approaches that rely solely on individual acoustic features face difficulties in fully exploiting the rich information embedded in speech signals. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel emotion recognition system based on a multi-level attention mechanism, which integrates both high-level textual features and multi-layered audio features for more effective emotion classification. By incorporating information from diverse modalities, this approach aims to improve recognition accuracy, addressing the shortcomings of single-modality systems. Experimental evaluations on the IEMOCAP and CASIA datasets confirm that our method successfully captures the intricate relationships between multi-level features, enabling refined information processing and significantly boosting model performance, thus providing a strong competitive edge.

articleTitle: Harnessing Large Language Models for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting with Multi-view Prompting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In recent years, Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) have attracted considerable attention from researchers. An important research direction is forecasting future events in TKGs based on historical information, i.e. TKG forecasting. Existing methods primarily rely on modeling temporal relationships between entity IDs to make predictions, which brings limitations in understanding the entity content and the relationships between entities. Fortunately, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has brought new insights into solving this problem. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-enhAnced TKG forEcasting (LATE) model. Specifically, we first design multi-view prompts that enable LLMs to generate comprehensive descriptions for entities as external knowledge. Then, we get the enhanced representations of entities based on the descriptions and we further design a contrastive learning strategy to reinforce this process. Finally, we construct a TKG forecasting model based on self-attention mechanisms and dual-pattern LSTM-based temporal modeling to accomplish the forecasting task. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our model compared with several state-of-the-art baseline methods.

articleTitle: Online Driving Style Analysis Based on Genetic Algorithm and CatBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Accurate driving behavior analysis can not only greatly improve driving safety and driver comfort, but also facilitate the development of trajectory planning, abnormal driving detection and other applications. The previous driving style analysis required the complete timing data of the driver, which could not be extracted in real time. This paper presents an online driving style analysis method, which is mainly divided into two parts. The first part is driving data segmentation and clustering based on K-means and genetic algorithm. Different subsequences are obtained by sliding window segmentation. The total KL divergence within the cluster is taken as the objective function, and the sub-sequence clustering results are obtained by genetic algorithm. Then, according to the final clustering results, the driving style of drivers is measured from three dimensions: statistical index, cospin similarity and KL divergence. The second part is the online driving primitive extraction model. According to the clustering results (labeled data) obtained in the first part, different machine learning models are trained, and the performance of random forest, KNN, SVM and CatBoost models is compared. Through the trained machine learning model, we are able to extract driving primitives in real time. The experimental results show that the first part can extract driving primitive and analyze driving style, and the second part CatBoost achieves better results than other machine learning models, with prediction accuracy of 0. 8, recall rate of 0. 82 and f1_score of 0. 81.

articleTitle: Thermophysical Properties Evaluation of Water Based Al2O3/TiO2 Hybrid Nanofluids: Experimental and ANN predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: A new type of nanofluid, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, were dispersed and stabilised into the water base fluid. In the present investigation, we have synthesised 50 wt.% Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles. Based on the experimental results, an equation of the general regression form was obtained.

articleTitle: AD-Gaussian: an Audio Driven Face Synthesis Method Leveraging Differential Attention and 3D Gaussian Splatting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper presents AD-Gaussian, a novel audio-driven face synthesis method. It efficiently integrates multiple input modalities—audio, blinking, and head movements, while employing differential attention to guide specific spatial regions to focus on the critical features that drive their visual changes. By dynamically predicting the deformation of 3D Gaussians, the method enables visually coherent face animations synchronized with speech. Experimental results show that AD-Gaussian outperforms existing methods on key metrics for rendering quality and synchronization accuracy while maintaining real-time performance.

articleTitle: Dense Semantic Mapping Method for Dynamic Workshop Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The intelligentization of workshops is a key direction for the smart transformation of the manufacturing industry. Autonomous navigation of intelligent mobile robots in dynamic workshop environments raises higher requirements for environmental perception and map building. Therefore, this paper proposes a dense semantic map construction algorithm suitable for dynamic workshop scenarios. The algorithm is based on the ORB- SLAM2 framework, combined with a lightweight semantic segmentation network, dynamic target elimination technology, and a dense semantic mapping thread, significantly improving the system's localization accuracy, map-building precision, and robustness. A dynamic elimination strategy is proposed by integrating optical flow, multi-view geometry constraints, and region growing methods with semantic priors, effectively reducing the interference from dynamic objects. Experimental results show that, compared to ORB-SLAM2, the algorithm proposed in this paper reduces the RMS error (RSME) and standard deviation (Std) of the Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) by 82.02% and 81.26%, respectively, and the RMS error and standard deviation of Relative Pose Error (RPE) by 39.40% and 36.23%, respectively, on the TUM public dataset. By utilizing keyframe dynamic region elimination and generating point clouds based on poses, semantic information is embedded into the dense map. Furthermore, the map's readability and clarity are optimized through the use of an octree structure, resulting in an accurate, robust, and semantically enriched dense map, which provides strong support for workshop intelligentization and the execution of high-level robotic tasks.

articleTitle: DynMLP-GNN : A Dynamic Sampling Graph Neural Network with Multi-Layer Perceptron for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Knowledge graphs have emerged as a pivotal area of research because of their extensive applications in personalized recommendations, drug interaction predictions, and intelligent question-answering systems. The existing methods based on graph neural networks use fixed propagation methods in knowledge graph inference, which often leads to information overload and reduces inference efficiency. To address this issue, this study introduces a novel graph neural network model, referred to as DynMLP-GNN, to enhance entity representations and improve path selection in knowledge graph reasoning. Specifically, this study incorporates an enhanced message-passing mechanism via multilayer perceptron, proposes a dynamic sampling strategy to prioritize entities most relevant to the query during propagation, and employs LSTM gating units to capture long-distance dependencies. Experimental results on multiple public knowledge graph datasets reveal that DynMLP-GNN substantially outperforms existing approaches in terms of both efficiency sand accuracy, particularly in addressing complex reasoning tasks.

articleTitle: Sliding Window Online Anomaly Detection for Dynamic Systems with Unsupervised Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Online Anomaly detection in operational data from dynamic systems is challenging due to the inherent complexity and variability of these datasets. This research introduces an innovative approach that leverages the Sliding Window Online Anomaly Detection method combined with online learning to enhance unsupervised algorithms for online anomaly detection within time-series operational data. Compared to traditional offline anomaly detection models, this method offers a significant advantage by allowing the training set to be updated incrementally in real-time. Several unsupervised algorithms were evaluated under different conditions: insertion of outliers, insertion of random noise and real fault data. Our method shows that traditional time-series data anomaly detection algorithms can be further optimized in conjunction with online learning to perform well in dynamic systems.

articleTitle: Design of Fertilizer Analysis System for Precision Fertilizer Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The traditional fertilizer application method relies on experience to apply fertilizer on a large scale, which has problems such as fertilizer waste and environmental pollution, and affects the sustainable development of agriculture. For this reason, this paper designs and realizes a set of precision fertilizer application control systems containing sensors, decision-making, and positioning systems. Among them, the sensor system senses the real-time crop and soil status through soil moisture sensors, temperature sensors, and crop growth sensors; the decision-making system uses a high-performance processor, a variety of data transmission interfaces, data processing, and storage modules, and decision-making algorithm execution units to process and analyze the sensor data and generate the decision of fertilizer application. The localization system is based on the hardware of LIDAR, development boards, etc., as well as the SLAM map building, and AMCL positioning algorithm to achieve accurate positioning; through these three systems to fully regulate the fertilization to achieve precision fertilization.

articleTitle: Sensor packaging method based on the solid tire sole of wheel-legged robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: For wheel-legged robots, the unique wheel-legged structure significantly influences the dynamics and kinematic behavior of the foot during ground contact. This paper presents a resistive strain gauge sensor integration scheme for solid tires, wherein sensors are embedded within the tires to actively monitor the touchdown information of the foot-end. A method is proposed for embedding the solid tires in circumferential arrays to capture the plantar strain state, which supports the control system of wheel-legged robots. To evaluate the effectiveness of this sensor package, a simulated impact experiment was conducted to simulate the wheel-legged ground contact. The experimental results demonstrate that the strain gauge embedding method effectively detects the strain response of solid tires under impact. Since ground contact information is crucial for the autonomous switching of the wheel-legged structure in robots, the successful implementation of this sensing system for ground contact monitoring holds significant potential for both research and practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Emotions in Artworks using EfficientNet Convolutional Network Integrating the Gram Matrix Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of an automatic assessment of emotions in artworks. This is a really important question because it can be extended not only to the emotions of artworks but also to the emotions of the environment around us. The EfficientNet convolutional neural network implementation, integrating the Gram matrix modules, was chosen for the problem. In previous studies, such a solution proved effective for analyzing emotions in images of a general nature. Four image datasets with the known emotion of a particular image were used to find the most appropriate one for the problem. The probabilities with which the neural network assigns emotions to the test art images are estimated. We see significant differences between these probability values. The small probability values obtained allow us to determine which emotions are not inherent in a given image. This is only initial research, as art is perceived subjectively, and the human factor is integral to the solution. However, its results are promising.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization strategy of YOLOv8 target detection model based on scene adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This study focuses on the target detection task in the automatic driving scene. Aiming at the deficiency of the traditional YOLOv8 model in complex scene adaptability, a scenario-based YOLOv8 target detection model is proposed. Through the design of scene classification module, multi-branch YOLOv8 model and dynamic parameter adjustment strategy, combined with data enhancement, model fusion and optimization technology, the detection accuracy and generalization ability of the model in different scenarios are effectively improved. In the experiment, BDD100K data set was used for training and testing, and the results showed that the method significantly improved the detection performance in bad weather and low light environment, and provided strong support for the development of autonomous driving technology.

articleTitle: Path planning of RRT-Connect robotic arm based on Beetle Antennae algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of large randomness, many redundant nodes, and long search time in path planning of the RRT-Connect algorithm in searching, an improved RRT-Connect algorithm was proposed. Improve search efficiency by adding a third point between the start and end point as a new extension point. Combined with the Beetle Antennae Search algorithm, the smell concentration capability sensed by the left and right antennae of the Beetle Antennae Search algorithm is brought into RRT-Connect to reduce the number of redundant points and accelerate the convergence speed. Simulation experiments of the original and improved RRT-Connect algorithm are carried out in 2D and 3D environments respectively, and the experiments show that it can effectively shorten the path length and reduce the search time. Finally, the effectiveness of the improved algorithm is verified by the simulation of the robotic arm.

articleTitle: UAV swarm network service classification based on multi-target threat assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The current research on UAV swarm network service classification ignores the impact of combat targets and their timeliness needs, this topic carries out the research on UAV swarm network service classification strategy based on multi-target threat assessment. Firstly, the network service classification attributes are analyzed in terms of service type, mission type, target threat classification, etc. Subsequently, multiple calculation methods of service classification attribute values are discussed; then, two network service classification calculation methods are given; finally, network service classification adjustment method and implementation strategy are introduced. The proposed method can take into account the needs of the business layer, which helps to accomplish the task effectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Strategy Improved Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Robot Task Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Task allocation in multi-robot systems (MRTA) is a critical issue that needs to be addressed. The emerging Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) algorithm successfully integrates global extensive searching and local fine-tuning capabilities through its flexible search mechanism. In an effort to optimize the capabilities and investigate the applicability of DBO in MRTA scenarios, we developed an advanced variant called Multi-Strategy Improved Dung Beetle Optimization (IDBO). The initialization phase incorporates a chaos-based mapping technique, which is used to create an initial population with more uniform distribution and enhanced diversity. To achieve an optimal balance between exploration and exploitation capabilities, the algorithm implements a nonlinear convergence coefficient when updating the locations of both breeding and small dung beetles. A simulated annealing strategy is implemented in the position updating of theft beetles, which helps prevent the algorithm from falling into local optima. Finally, the improved algorithm, along with the DBO and Genetic Algorithm (GA), is applied to MRTA in a warehouse environment for simulation experiments. The results demonstrate that the IDBO algorithm achieves higher and faster convergence accuracy and has a better capability to escape local optima, showing superior performance in MRTA problems.

articleTitle: DGE-ASR: Two-view Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Knowledge graph completion aims to address knowledge gaps caused by difficulties in collecting real-world facts. This paper proposes a novel dual-view graph neural network model, DGE-ASR, which designs a dual isomorphic graph attention encoder. It separately constructs isomorphic graphs centered on entity nodes and relation nodes, and then aggregates important neighbor information on both graphs using graph attention networks. Although the node types in the two graphs differ, modeling the entity and relation perspectives separately captures the heterogeneity of the knowledge graph to some extent. During the encoding phase, quaternion operations are used to enhance the GNN layers, effectively modeling the complex interactions between entities and relations, as well as between relations and entities. Additionally, skip connections and residual connections are designed to mitigate the issues of oversmoothing and gradient vanishing in graph neural networks. Experimental results on six datasets (FB15K-237, CoDEx, LitWD1K) show that DGE-ASR outperforms existing GNN- based models and tensor decomposition methods.

articleTitle: A LSTM-Based Trajectory Prediction Method For Aerial Target
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The dynamic and accurate prediction of the target trajectory about UAVs is the key point of airspace management. For the task of air target trajectory prediction dominated by a variety of UAVs, traditional methods can not deal with conditions such as complex modeling, high computational cost, and poor model reusability. This paper proposes an air target trajectory prediction method based on sliding window Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The sliding window method is adopted to segment the target historical trajectory data. The LSTM can memorize historical information and effectively process long time series to predict the trajectory data of air targets at future moments. The prediction error comparison simulation experiment is carried out between the polynomial fitting model method and the method proposed, which proves that the proposed method improves the trajectory prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: TDOA Based Extended Kalman Filter Fusion Approach for UAV Localization in GPS-denied Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Attributable to its high precision and strong interference resistance capability, the ultra-wideband (UWB) positioning technology has been widely researched as a wireless positioning technology for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) in global positioning denied and satellite signals blocked areas. The reliability of a solitary sensory input source may be compromised in such environmental conditions. Nevertheless, the environment variation still increases the estimation complexity of the measurement noise for UWB sensors. On the other hand, the loosely synchronized clock between the sensor nodes also limits the positioning performance of the existing UWB system. A fused positioning method with a clock-offset-compensated time difference of arrival (TDOA) positioning algorithm and extended Kalman filter (EKF) is presented in this paper to address these issues. According to the simulation results, the proposed approach attains a centimeter-level accuracy (the 95th percentile error is 0.076 m) and improves the standard deviation to 0.033 m.

articleTitle: Optimizing Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) Protocol with Pigeon-inspired Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper uses a Pigeon-inspired Optimization algorithm (PIO) to optimize the traditional Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) protocol, and scenario-based validation is carried out in an oilfield using a digital communication tester. The uplink transmission packet loss rate and delay metrics before and after using the algorithm are tested and compared while ensuring that the RSRP and SINR are consistent. The results show that the FRER transmission after using PIO is more stable, and the uplink transmission packet loss rate and delay are better than the standard FRER transmission.

articleTitle: Efficient Techniques for Processing Medical Texts in Legal Documents Using Transformer Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The extensive utilisation of medical texts in legal documents has led to the emergence of a significant research topic: the development of efficient methods for processing these texts in order to extract key medical information. This paper puts forth an enhanced model based on the Transformer architecture with the objective of optimising the processing efficiency of medical texts in legal documents. Based on the existing Transformer model, we have devised a multi-level attention mechanism that combines multi-task learning and domain adaptation technology. This mechanism enables the simultaneous capture of the association between medical terms and legal language in the text, thereby enhancing the model's ability to comprehend complex legal language. Furthermore, domain knowledge graph-assisted training is employed to enhance the precise matching of medical and legal terminology by the model. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model markedly enhances the precision and efficiency of information extraction in diverse medical text processing tasks, outperforming the traditional model.

articleTitle: Research on Human Action Recognition Based on Edge Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Intelligent recognition algorithms deployed on edge devices offer strong real-time processing capabilities and high security for online video image analysis. However, real-time video image recognition remains challenging, particularly when deploying computationally intensive action recognition models on resource-constrained edge devices. This paper introduces a dual-network human action recognition method that leverages the strengths of both 2D and 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Initially, a 2D CNN detects hu-man targets, followed by the generation of time-sequence data for these tar-gets using a matching method. Human action recognition is then achieved through a 3D CNN. This method addresses the challenges of extracting and modeling temporal action characteristics, enabling accurate human action localization and classification. Five distinct action recognition datasets were constructed to train the 3D CNN, which were subsequently deployed on an edge intelligent platform. Empirical testing of the action recognition system demonstrated a recognition speed of 10 frames per second, with accuracy exceeding 80% for certain action categories.

articleTitle: pFedCE: Personalized Federated Learning Based on Contribution Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across clients without sharing raw data, ensuring privacy while utilizing decentralized data. However, the heterogeneous distribution of data among clients can significantly degrade the performance of the global model. To address this problem, we propose a personalized FL (pFL) framework pFedCE. Unlike traditional FL, pFedCE introduces a Shapley value-based contribution evaluation during model aggregation, adaptively adjusting aggregating weights based on contribution to generate a personalized aggregation model for each client. Since direct access to client data for contribution evaluation would violate principles of FL, we utilize a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate synthetic data on the server that preserve the statistical properties of client data. We evaluated pFedCE on three benchmark datasets in three types of data distribution. The results show that pFedCE outperforms six other pFL methods.

articleTitle: Environment Based Multi-Object Grasp Planning in Bin Picking Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Given the potential of bin picking to eliminate manual handing practices in manufacturing and logistics industries, this paper presents an environment-based grasp planning pipeline to address the challenges posed by complex object arrangements in cluttered environments. The pipeline integrates offline grasp planning system with online grasp filter, designed specifically for multi-object cluttered bin picking tasks. In the offline phase, the pipeline utilizes the improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to generate the grasp solutions by incorporating gripper and object models. In the online phase, the system considers grasp and robot kinematics to prioritize objects and determine the best grasp based on the grasp task scene model and the precomputed solutions from the offline phase. The proposed pipeline is validated through both simulated and experimental trials using the Franka Emika Panda robotic arm. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the pipeline in handling multi-object cluttered bin picking tasks.

articleTitle: A Multi-head Attention Transformer Framework for Oesophageal Cancer Survival Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Oesophageal cancer is one of the malignant tumours with poor prognosis and accurate survival prediction is important to guide clinical treatment decisions. However, existing prediction methods are difficult to effectively capture the complex interactions among clinical features and lack sufficient interpretability. To address these issues, we propose a survival prediction model for oesophageal cancer based on multi-head attention Transformer, which achieves adaptive capture and efficient representation of interactions between features through a 4-head attention mechanism and a 64-dimensional feature embedding space. Experiments on the TCGA-ESCA dataset (n=286) show that the model achieves 84.6%, 89.1% and 83.7% in the key metrics of accuracy, AUC-ROC and F1 score respectively, which are significantly better than existing methods. Characteristic importance analysis revealed that the age at first diagnosis, number of lymph nodes examined, and KPS score were the key factors affecting prognosis, providing an interpretable basis for clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Survey of Lightweight Object Detection Model Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have recently achieved significant success in many visual recognition tasks. However, these models suffer from being computationally expensive and memory intensive, hindering their deployment in devices with low memory resources or in applications with strict latency requirements. Therefore, studying and designing lightweight models is one of the current research hotspots. Building a lightweight object detection algorithm is a challenging task because the model must be carefully designed to minimize parameters and computing resources while achieving high detection performance. In the past 10 years, lightweight algorithm design has made significant progress. In this paper, we summarize lightweight object detection algorithms to further explore new ideas and directions for lightweight network design. This paper divides the lightweight algorithm design into three categories: backbone network, feature fusion network, and attention mechanism. For each category, this paper provides a detailed analysis of the performance, advantages, and limitations of the modules in the object detection task. Then, we briefly introduce some recent successful methods, such as the Mobilenet series and DETR. Finally, we conclude this paper and discuss the challenges and potential directions for future work. The development trend of lightweight design in the field of object detection is examined.

articleTitle: YOLO-DynamicNet: A Dynamic Network for Maritime Tiny Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Maritime object detection is a representative task of tiny object detection within a large field of view. The research on end-to-end object detection networks based on high-resolution images captured by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) further exacerbates the performance degradation of tiny object detection. The excellent YOLOv8 aim to achieve a balance between speed and performance on the benchmark, such as COCO. For the series of YOLO model, the detection of medium and large objects is much excellent, but the detection of tiny objects is given relatively less consideration. To this end, we proposed the YOLO-DynamicNet based on the YOLOv8 to enhance the detection performance of maritime tiny objects. The improved model consists various improvements, such as a tiny object detection layer, the optimization of CSP layer based on dynamic convolution, and the application of dynamic upsampler and dynamic head. The experiments are implemented on the popular SeaDronesSee dataset. The dynamic ability of the network for feature extraction and the improvement of model expressive capacity are demonstrated. YOLO-DynamicNet improves the performance of detecting maritime tiny objects with a relatively small increasing of parameters and computational cost. Compared with the baseline, the performance of the proposed dynamic model is improved by 8.6% in terms of mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>. Regarding the three typical maritime objects of swimmer, lifesaving appliances, and buoy, the performance is improved by 5.3%, 16.8%, and 18.7% respectively in terms of mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Gait Recognition Method with Self-attention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In today’s era, gait recognition has received extensive attention due to its excellent anti-counterfeiting, accurate recognition effect and flexible application. The development of this recognition method has received great attention. The recognition of gait data by artificial intelligence algorithm is helpful to observe, predict and effectively use motion data. Currently, The computer vision recognition technology and radar-based limb motion recognition technology has been widely used for gait recognition. However, the existing technologies exhibit limitations in terms of recognition range and insufficient recognition accuracy. But there is an increasing demand for comprehensive and accurate gait recognition technology. Therefore, improving various indicators of gait recognition has become a rather popular and important research direction today.

articleTitle: An Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm for UAV 3D Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: For the problem of three-dimensional path planning for UAVs, an improved PSO(Particle Swarm Optimization) is proposed by improving the existing model. For the model, the Analytic Hierarchy Process is used to determine the weight parameters for the objective function. In terms of algorithm, firstly, the population will be initialized at a higher altitude range pair to increase the number of effective particles in the pre-population; secondly, for the drawback of particle swarm algorithm that is easy to fall into local optimum, the inertia parameter is processed by linear varying, and an additional population is set up to enhance the exploration and development in the full cycle of the algorithm; moreover, in order to carry out the exploration and development in a better way, a real-time updating elite population is proposed which can record multiple optimal particles in the environment. The experimental results show that compared with the original algorithm, the IPSO(Improved Particle Swarm Optimization) improves the convergence speed and optimization performance.

articleTitle: Variational Multi-Scale Feature Integration for Few- Shot Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Traditional few-shot object detection(FSOD) models are typically trained on benchmark datasets such as PASCAL VOC 2007+2012 and MS COCO 2014. However, these datasets exhibit significant limitations in terms of scale distribution and target density, making it challenging for models trained on them to perform well in multi-scale scenarios, especially when detecting dense small objects. As a result, models trained on these datasets often struggle with sensitivity to scale variations, reducing their effectiveness in handling complex multi-scale object detection tasks. To address this issue, we utilize the VisDrone2019 dataset, which features a wide range of scale distributions and significant scale variability, and construct a FSOD dataset from it. Based on this dataset, we integrate Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and their variants into the classical FSOD framework Meta R-CNN. This integration significantly enhances the model's capability to model fine-grained feature distributions of support samples and improves robustness through variational feature generation. Furthermore, we incorporate Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) and their variants to optimize multi-scale object feature representations, achieving notable improvements in performance for multi-scale object detection. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches on the VisDrone2019 few-shot object detection dataset, showcasing significant advantages in addressing multi-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Smooth Path Planning of Logistics Robot based on improved Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: A better ant colony algorithm was created to fix the issues with the old one when it comes to planning the paths of logistics robots in a two-dimensional grid environment. These issues include a slow convergence speed, too many stopping points, and an easy tendency to get stuck in a local optimal state. To begin, the heuristic function of the artificial potential field gravity is changed so that it is affected by the goal point. This makes it easier to find the best path and speed up the convergence process. Next, the difference in pheromone concentration between the last round's best path and worst path was added to the pheromone. The pheromone concentration was then changed to make the search path as long as possible. The triangular pruning method is also used to get rid of unnecessary stopping points, cut down on the number of turns the robot has to make, and make sure the planned path is smoother and easier for the logistics robot to follow. The results of the experiment show that the improved ant colony algorithm makes the best path length, path transition times, and convergence speed 3.9%, 33%, and 66.7% better than the method suggested in paper [16]. It has been shown that the improved ant colony algorithm is good at planning paths on a world level.

articleTitle: A Novel Fingerprint Recognition Strategy Driven by Convolutional Autoencoders and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper investigates a fingerprint recognition method based on Convolutional Autoencoder, aimed at integrating the advantages of fingerprint ridge and minutiae information to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of fingerprint feature extraction and matching. To achieve this, we propose a novel fixed-length local fingerprint embedding extraction method. This method is modified based on the Convolutional Autoencoder framework and incorporates an attention mechanism, significantly boosting the model's ability to capture latent information and detailed features beneficial for fingerprint matching. Furthermore, we employ fingerprint masks to refine local descriptors, thereby mitigating the adverse impact of nonoverlapping fingerprint regions on matching. Through experiments conducted on multiple datasets, our method surpasses the performance of the currently advanced fingerprint recognition system AFRNet, excelling particularly in handling low-quality and highly similar fingerprints. Additionally, the method demonstrates remarkable performance in fingerprint reconstruction tasks, providing a new solution for enhancing low- quality fingerprints. Finally, the paper concludes with a summary of the research findings and an outlook on future research directions.

articleTitle: Multidimensional data processing and estimation algorithm for pipeline settlement measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the rapid development of our country’s economy, the density of urban pipe network has increased continuously. These pipeline lines operate in the environment of long transportation distance, large span and complex geological conditions. Due to the complexity of the environment, they are easily affected by geological disasters, and the settlement or even damage of pipelines may lead to direct and indirect secondary disasters, which will bring great impact on society and economy. The application of RFID based IoT sensing system in underground pipeline management realizes real-time monitoring of pipeline settlement displacement by burying devices carrying RFID tags underground, preventing economic losses and social disasters. Combined with BeiDou positioning technology, the system provides high-precision positioning and deformation monitoring, making positive contributions to the safe operation of urban infrastructure. The technology is expected to become an important tool for underground pipeline management and promote social stability and sustainable development.

articleTitle: LLM Intelligent Customer Service in Property Management Using a RAG Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Traditional property management services often struggle with challenges such as long response times and difficulties in effectively addressing complex tenant issues. While Large Language Models (LLMs), like ChatGPT, offer promising solutions, they are often limited by their lack of domain-specific knowledge, leading to inaccurate or irrelevant responses. To address these shortcomings, this paper introduces an intelligent customer service system tailored for property management. The system integrates a customized LLM with the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, designed to provide accurate, context-aware, and personalized responses. By employing an intelligent agent to pull relevant data from a dedicated property management knowledge base, the system can engage tenants in real-time through an interactive interface, ensuring both efficiency and relevance in communication. Additionally, machine learning algorithms are employed to continuously improve the system’s performance. The architecture combines a fine-tuned LLM, a vector database for fast information retrieval, and a feedback loop that supports ongoing optimization. We anticipate that this approach will lead to greater tenant satisfaction, more personalized services, and enhanced operational efficiency. This study contributes to the broader fields of Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication by showcasing how RAG can be applied to improve customer service, with future work focusing on real-world implementation and comprehensive system evaluation.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Secure Transmission for NOMA-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the challenges of limited network access and reduced scalability in cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks due to users sharing the same time-frequency resource blocks, secure transmission using non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) was studied. Physical layer security issues like pilot spoofing and meeting varying security requirements by categorizing user devices as secure or regular were tackled. The research considered the use of a conjugate beamforming precoder under short-term power constraints and implemented successive interference cancellation (SIC) in the downlink. Closed-form expressions for the achievable ergodic rate of users and the upper bound of the ergodic eavesdropping capacity were derived. The network security performance was evaluated in detail by the achievable secrecy rate and sum achievable secrecy rate. Simulation results confirmed that NOMA technology significantly boosts user access capacity. However, the SIC in NOMA systems has a cumulative effect, emphasizing the need for precise SIC implementation to achieve secure transmission in NOMA-aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO networks.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Time-Slot Scheduling and Beamforming for Cooperative Satellites with Per-Antenna Power Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the time-slot user scheduling and beamforming design for cooperative satellites. We take into account the more practical constraint of per-antenna power constraint (PAPC). Unlike traditional approaches where these two issues are usually studied separately, we adopt a joint optimization strategy to maximize the max-min fairness (MMF) spectral efficiency of the cooperative satellite system. Thus, we formulate the MMF problem to optimize time-slot user scheduling and beamforming design. We first obtain the decoupling problem of the initial problem through equivalent transformation in order to reduce its complexity. Then, we proposed an efficient convex relaxation method based on the successive convex approximation (SCA) and semi-definite relaxation (SDR) technique to solve the decoupled problem. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed joint optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: The Enhanced vision-language model developing for fine-grained difficult sample classification tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In special practical scenarios such as severe weather and dense buildings, intelligent target recognition relying on single modal images faces problems of image occlusion and blurring. Especially for fine-grained targets, the classification accuracy will significantly decrease. Based on the complementary characteristics of multimodal information, an enhanced vision-language model for fine-grained target recognition is proposed (DS-VL+). The experimental results show that randomly deactivating modal information during the training process and using feature fusion and decision fusion methods for target recognition, can effectively address the problem of modal loss. This article also proposes a method for constructing the difficult sample dataset that simulates complex real-world data situations, and constructs two datasets: Difficulty-CUB and Difficulty-Flower. The influence of difficult samples on the accuracy of single mode classification algorithm is analyzed on these two data sets. The classification accuracy of this model on fine-grained difficult samples can be comparable to that of unimodal models on general samples, while surpassing existing image language classification models and achieving SOTA.

articleTitle: Blind SR: Semantic-assisted Spatially-Varying Blur Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Low-Resolution (LR) images resulted from object motion or camera defocus generally have space-variant blur kernels. Traditional blind Super-Resolution (SR) reconstruction methods fail to consider this variability, resulting in subpar performance in practical applications. To address this issue, this paper introduces a multi-task learning framework and proposes a Semantic-Enhanced Blur Prediction Network (SEBPN). With blur prediction as the primary task, we incorporate a Cross-Spatial Interaction (CSI) network and an Improved Grouping Interactive Attention (Improved-GIA) module as dual-feature fusion network to effectively utilize both blur and semantic features. The CSI network enables feature interactions across different scales and stages, extending receptive field by introducing positional information and convolutional kernels of varying sizes. This extension enhances the network's sensitivity to spatial details, allowing it to more accurately capture regions with spatially varying blur. Additionally, we inrtoduce coordinate attention to improve the fusion of dual features, significantly boosting blur prediction accuracy. This enhancement, which combined with existing non-blind Super-Resolution reconstruction method, leads to higher-quality reconstructed images. This paper utilizes the NYUv2-BSR and Cityscapes-BSR datasets, which proposed by CMOS in space-variant blur domain, and conducts qualitative and quantitative experiments with the most advanced methods on real images. Results demonstrate the superiority of our approach, leading to state-of-the-art blind SR performance.

articleTitle: Auto-tuning of Large-Scale Parallel Computing Applications Based on Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The performance of large-scale parallel computing applications is highly dependent on the parameter settings within complex systems. Due to the high-dimensional and nonlinear nature of kernel environment parameter spaces, traditional manual tuning methods are both labor-intensive and inefficient when exploring optimal parameter combinations, often leading to suboptimal performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes an automated parameter tuning framework based on Bayesian optimization, aimed at efficiently exploring complex high-dimensional parameter spaces and predicting better-performing parameter combinations. This framework builds a surrogate model, iteratively selects potentially efficient parameter configurations, and integrates SHAP to analyze the influence of each parameter on performance optimization. We validated the effectiveness of this framework in several typical large-scale parallel computing application scenarios, including NAS Parallel Benchmarks (NPB), quantum chemistry simulation software Quantum ESPRESSO and VASP, and the Weather Research and Forecasting model (WRF). Experimental results show that Bayesian optimization significantly shortens the overall tuning time and performs traditional methods such as genetic algorithms in terms of performance optimization. Experimental results show that Bayesian optimization significantly shortens the overall tuning time by 50% and improves application performance by up to 11%, outperforming traditional methods such as genetic algorithms in terms of performance optimization. Furthermore, SHAP analysis reveals the importance of key kernel parameters in enhancing application performance.

articleTitle: A Spatial-Temporal Trajectory Planner for Center-articulated Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In this paper, a new local trajectory planning algorithm for center-articulated vehicles (CAVs) is proposed to generate safe and collision-free trajectories in structured or semistructured scenarios. The method is based on an optimization framework that is able to maintain high-precision constraints on the motion while ensuring safe obstacle avoidance. By converting the planning problem into an optimal control problem (OCP) and modeling the environment with irregular safety corridors, we are able to fully utilize the available space while ensuring safe obstacle avoidance. In addition, by eliminating all equality and inequality constraints, we reformulate the problem as an unconstrained optimization problem to accelerate the solution process. Simulation results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of efficiency, speed of solution, and safe obstacle avoidance. In order to promote the open-source community, we have made the project engineering open-source on [https://github.com/Photin1a/LoaderPlanner.git].

articleTitle: FedDPC: A Density Peak Clustering-based Federated Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is widely applied in edge computing scenarios to protect data privacy, but the assumption of independent and identically distributed (IID) data across clients often does not hold in practice, leading to performance degradation. Among the many methods proposed to address data heterogeneity, clustered federated learning (CFL) has emerged as a popular approach. Current CFL methods commonly adopt the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm, which mitigates the problem of data heterogeneity. However, they still face challenges such as requiring more clients than traditional federated learning and introducing randomness in the clustering process. To overcome these limitations, we propose FedDPC, which integrates the density peak clustering (DPC) algorithm. This approach provides the advantages of not requiring additional clients and having a non-random partitioning strategy. Finally, we conducted experiments to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been extensively researched and used in both academia and industry since the rise in popularity of the Transformer model, which demonstrates excellent performance in AI. However, the computational demands of LLMs are immense, and the energy resources required to run them are often limited. For instance, popular models like GPT-3, with 175 billion parameters and a storage requirement of 350 GB, present significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained IoT devices and embedded systems. These systems often lack the computational capacity to handle such large models. Quantization, a technique that reduces the precision of model values to a smaller set of discrete values, offers a promising solution by reducing the size of LLMs and accelerating inference. In this research, we provide a comprehensive analysis of quantization techniques within the machine learning field, with a particular focus on their application to LLMs. We begin by exploring the mathematical theory of quantization, followed by a review of common quantization methods and how they are implemented. Furthermore, we examine several prominent quantization methods applied to LLMs, detailing their algorithms and performance outcomes.

articleTitle: Improved PSO Parameter Identification-Based Composite STSM Controller for BLDC Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: This paper designs a composite super-twisting sliding mode(STSM) controller for brushless direct current motor (BLDC) based on an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm for parameter identification. The conventional sliding mode surface is enhanced to a non-singular integral terminal sliding mode surface, and a composite STSM control strategy is introduced, which boasts the advantages of reduced chattering, rapid convergence, and minimal influence from external disturbances. Additionally, to address the issue of rotor inertia affecting controller performance, an improved PSO algorithm is employed for identification. This improved PSO algorithm optimizes the inertia weight by incorporating the distance between the particle's best position and the swarm's global best position and enhances the individual and social learning factors with hyperbolic functions, resulting in high precision and fast identification speed.

articleTitle: The Research Progress on Teleoperation and Interactive Control Technology of Power Operation Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: As the operational demands of power systems grow, the application of teleoperated robots in the power sector has advanced. Traditional live-line robots have improved inspection efficiency and accuracy, while new teleoperated robots integrate technologies such as force feedback, immersive visual interaction, and deep learning. These innovations enable natural human-machine interaction, precise control, and intelligent analysis. This paper summarizes key technologies in teleoperation and interaction control for power operation robots and outlines future trends, including multi-channel teleoperation based on force feedback. Future developments will focus on multi-channel shared control and power big model-assisted operation, with closer integration with computer graphics, enhancing both operator-robot interaction and the robots' decision-making and operational precision.

articleTitle: Potential-Intent Graph Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have exhibited significant efficacy in the representation of users and items within recommender systems. This exceptional performance is largely attributed to their ability to aggregate collaborative information from higher-order neighbors, thereby improving the optimization of embedding representations. However, with GCN-based models, node embeddings become similar when stacking too many layers, making them indistinguishable, which is known as the over-smoothing problem. We believe that an important element of the over-smoothing problem is that the multiple potential intentions a user may possess—such as merely passing time or selecting a gift for another individual—during the convolution of the multi-layer graph. For this reason, we propose a Potential-Intent Aware GCN-based recommendation model. This model effectively captures multiple potential intentions of users and constructs a set of sub-graphs comprising users with analogous interests. Then, the model performs higher-order graph convolution within these subgraphs. To evaluate the performance of the model, we conduct extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, and the results indicating that our model outperforms existing GCN-based recommendation models.

articleTitle: Post-Quantum Cryptography and TEE for 5G VPN in Power Systems: Assessment and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The power industry is critically dependent on reliable and secure communication networks for operations such as remote monitoring, real-time scheduling, and smart meter data upload. With the expansion of distributed energy resources, traditional private networks are increasingly insufficient, making the flexible and widely covered public 5G networks a vital alternative. However, the openness of public 5G networks also exposes them to numerous security threats, including data eavesdropping, identity spoofing, and man-in-the-middle attacks. This study addresses these challenges by proposing a comprehensive security access framework that integrates advanced cryptographic technologies, Trusted Execution Environments (TEE), and blockchain to ensure data transmission security, access control reliability, and communication process privacy within public 5G networks for power industry applications. The framework’s innovations include designing network layer security access mechanisms with VPN and tunneling technologies, constructing application layer post-quantum cryptographic solutions, and proposing terminal layer trusted protection strategies. The integration of these technologies aims to enhance the resilience and efficiency of power systems while maintaining high standards of security in public 5G environments.

articleTitle: An Aerospace Equipment Operation and Maintenance Scheduling Method Based on LLM and Solver
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated management approach was proposed for aerospace equipment maintenance based on large language models (LLMs) and optimization solvers, aiming to improve the efficiency and convenience of maintenance decision support. A dataset tailored to maintenance scenarios in the aerospace domain was constructed, and the GLM4-9B model was fine-tuned using the LoRA method to accurately understand and invoke maintenance task instructions. Combining the OR-Tools optimization solver, a two-stage algorithm was designed to optimize maintenance resource allocation and vehicle routing. On this basis, a prototype system for integrated maintenance management based on LLMs and optimization solvers is implemented, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The proposed method was demonstrated by experimental results to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of maintenance decision-making in the aerospace domain, offering new insights for aerospace equipment maintenance management.

articleTitle: Structure Design of Adaptive Probabilistic Modular Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: To address the challenge of online modular neural networks being unable to efficiently handle high-dimensional data in real-time, this paper proposes an Adaptive Probability Modular Neural Network (APMNN). Firstly, the parameters of each Gaussian component within the model are updated in real-time based on probability density, enhancing the network's ability to adapt to time-varying data and improving clustering quality, thereby achieving online partitioning of the sample space. Secondly, through probability membership sets, condition data of different components are assigned to the corresponding subnetworks for learning. Finally, ensemble weights are used to integrate the outputs of different subnetworks to obtain the final prediction results. Predictions on artificial datasets demonstrate that this network can effectively partition high-dimensional data in real-time, achieving higher accuracy and a more streamlined structure compared to traditional modular neural networks.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks: Key Challenges for Security Defense in the Age of Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has revolutionized various industries. However, the vulnerability of deep learning models, which are the core technology of AI, has been gradually exposed, among which adversarial attacks have become a prominent security issue. Adversarial attacks pose a threat to the reliability of AI systems by adding tiny perturbations to the input data to mislead the model and lead to wrong prediction results. This paper offers an exhaustive overview of adversarial attacks, encompassing their definitions, taxonomies, and the methodologies for crafting adversarial examples. A comparative analysis of the strengths and weaknesses inherent to different adversarial examples generation techniques is presented, alongside an exposition of their critical influence on the security landscape of deep learning technologies. Finally, the discourse concludes with a prospective outlook on the evolving trends in adversarial attacks.

articleTitle: Hotel Service Robot Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the advancement of technology and the growing demand for intelligent and efficient services, the traditional hotel service model is increasingly unable to meet people's expectations for personalized and non-contact experiences. In this context, this study proposes an STM32-based control system for hotel service robots. The system integrates motor control, voice recognition, touch screen interaction and an innovative doorbell module to improve service quality. It also runs the bidirectional A* path planning algorithm with the help of Raspberry Pi, which enables the robot to navigate autonomously in complex hotel environments and perform precise food delivery and guest guidance tasks. Experimental results show that this system can improve the service efficiency of hotels and reduce the waste of laboratory resources in the traditional hotel industry, thus promoting the transformation of traditional hotels into smart hotels, while improving customer experience, attracting more guests and enhancing the competitiveness of hotels.

articleTitle: Many-Objective Evolutionary Optimization Algorithm based on the Conflict Measurement Grouping Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: In order to address the convergence issues faced by traditional multi-objective optimization algorithms as the number of objectives increases, this paper proposes a new optimization algorithm, MaOEA-SPC, based on the conflict measurement grouping strategy. First, due to the inherent correlation between subproblems and many-objective optimization problems, we propose a conflict measurement grouping strategy to facilitate knowledge transfer. Next, we extract the distribution characteristics of Pareto solutions during the evolution process of subproblems to establish a Gaussian distribution model that serves as knowledge information. Subsequently, the new individuals generated by the distribution model are added to the population of MaOPs. Finally, the simulation results indicate that the MaOEA-SPC algorithm effectively enhances the convergence speed of MaOPs without lowering the quality of the solution.

articleTitle: Study on the Motion Characteristics of Micro-Robots in Complex Environments Based on the VACPO-Xgboost Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: With the rapid development of micro/nano-robot technology, these devices demonstrate broad application prospects in biomedical fields such as drug delivery, minimally invasive surgery, and disease detection. Traditional hydrodynamic models, based on simplified boundary conditions, fail to effectively simulate the complex boundary conditions in biomedical environments. This paper proposes a hybrid model that combines a variant algorithm based on Crested Porcupine Optimizer (VACPO) with Xgboost, termed the VACPO-Xgboost model, to optimize the prediction of the hydrodynamic behavior of micro-robots. Using the COMSOL Multiphysics simulation environment, this study investigates the impact of geometric features and surface velocity distribution on the motion of micro-robots. The proposed model accurately predicts the velocity of micro-robots under complex boundary conditions. Results indicate that the VACPO-XGBoost model significantly outperforms other machine learning algorithms in hydrodynamic prediction, achieving improvements across all three regression metrics, with RMSE reduced by 16.5% and MAE reduced by 16.2%, while exhibiting excellent robustness and showcasing its potential application value in complex biomedical scenarios. Additionally, SHAP-based analysis effectively reveals the contributions of individual features to the model's output, providing deeper insights into how input features influence micro-robot motion in complex fluid environments. This offers strong support for the optimized design and precise control of micro-robots.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation and Parameter Simplification for Power Operation and Maintenance-based LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: The large language models (LLMs) have great potential for application in the field of power operation and maintenance. Unlike previous single visual models, the visual big model has shown great advantages in image understanding with its massive multi-modal information and huge network parameters. However, due to the huge number of parameters in the current general visual big models, it is difficult to deploy them on site and there are few practical applications. Therefore, this article proposes knowledge distillation and model pruning for power-specific models. After general visual big models and data processing, high-quality pseudo-label data is obtained, and knowledge distillation is used to obtain a student model with fewer parameters. Then, the student model is sparsely trained and pruned, and fine-tuned on the power data set to obtain an easy-to-deploy lightweight power-specific model. Finally, a student model with a parameter volume of 100 million to 1 billion is obtained through knowledge distillation. Through model pruning, the model is compressed to more than 50% of the volume before pruning, and the model detection rate drops by no more than 1%, effectively improving the efficiency of the model.

articleTitle: Test-Time training for domain adaption in IP geolocation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
abstract: IP geolocation is a fundamental task in network management and cybersecurity, enabling services such as targeted advertising and content delivery optimization. However, the performance of geolocation models often deteriorates due to distribution shifts between training and testing data, such as changes in network topologies, new IP address allocations, or the emergence of previously unseen geographical regions. These challenges make it difficult for traditional geolocation models to generalize effectively in real-world scenarios. To tackle this issue, we introduce TTAGeo, a novel approach that applies test-time adaptation (TTA) techniques to dynamically adjust model parameters during inference. Our method integrates empirical risk minimization and self-supervised learning (SSL) to adapt geolocation models in a flexible and efficient manner.
